events.title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
events.blurb: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers with David Hughes.

events.title: Luna Loves the Festival with Joseph Coelho & Fiona Lumbers
events.blurb: She loves scouring library bookshelves, digging in gardens, dancing, and looking at famous art. And now Luna’s giving sports a go in Luna Loves Sport. Curious, creative, imaginative, and affirming, the Luna Loves books are family favourites as Joseph Coelho’s poetic storytelling and Fiona Lumbers’ magical illustrations bring the power of connection and self-expression to life. Settle in for a friendly, interactive event – perfect for curious little ones.

events.title: Anne Enright: Attention
events.blurb: For 30 years, Anne Enright has been paying attention – to literature, to Ireland, to the voices and bodies of women – and writing about it all in prose so insightful and exuberant you want to dog-ear every page. Attention: Writing on Life, Art, and The World gathers a career's worth of essays on topics ranging from Dublin to Honduras, James Joyce to Toni Morrison. Today, the Booker Prize-winning author of The Gathering and The Green Road discusses craft, memory, and the art of looking closely with Caoilinn Hughes.

events.title: The More You Know with the National Museum of Scotland
events.blurb: How does a cyclops become a mammoth, or a tiger become a cat? Come and find out in this drop-in session with our brilliant pals from the National Museum of Scotland. Get hands-on and find out how we’re always learning new things about the past, then discover more about the prehistoric animals in the Museum’s Giants exhibition and what on earth it means to be a palaeontologist!

events.title: Welcome to Sparkleopolis with Rashmi Sirdeshpande
events.blurb: Sparkleopolis is a city that’s bright, busy, and fun, but it’s like parties – sometimes, it can just be a bit much. That’s why we need a superhero like Rashmi Sirdeshpande’s Super Uma! Her strength isn’t laser vision, she doesn’t have a cape – she just notices things, she listens, she cares, and that can really help to solve people’s problems. Come and meet Rashmi and brilliant illustrator Nakul P. who'll be there to show how to make your drawings the sparkliest ever!

events.title: The Great Big Story Show
events.blurb: Let’s get this Festival staaar-tedddd! We’re bringing together authors, storytellers, and poets for a fun-packed hour of stories, games, and very (very!) silly challenges. Who will create the creepiest creature, or write the best poem about moustaches? Find out today, peek at some of the best books on the block, AND be in with the chance of winning a prize! Amazing. Featuring the brilliant skills Vivian French, Hazel Darwin-Clements, Macastory and the Loud Poets' Katie Ailes.

events.title: Close Read with Open Book: Poems to Change Your Mind
events.blurb: Join Marjorie Lotfi and Jess Orr from Open Book, a charity organising shared reading and creative writing groups, as they introduce you to some of the brilliant poets appearing at this year’s Festival. The session will focus on poems from a range of perspectives, all in conversation with our hero theme, Changing Your Mind. No preparation required, reading materials will be provided. Expect an open discussion from the start.

events.title: Open House
events.blurb: You’re invited to our Open House! Bring your friends and join Festival director Jenny Niven and Festival guests as they take you through highlights of 2026: from the themes underpinning the programme and the stories behind our fantastic commissions to this year’s hidden gems. There’s so much to take in, so let Niven and our guests be your helpful guide across the next 16 days. Orlando Swayne and Len Pennie have joined this event. Chaired by Zara Janjua.

events.title: Stories & Crafts with Edinburgh for Under Fives
events.blurb: The team from that parental lifesaver, Edinburgh for Under Fives, is back to entertain little ones with a story and art activity to take home. All are welcome!

events.title: Len Pennie & Sophia Smith Galer: Use It or Lose It
events.blurb: When a language disappears, what else are we at risk of losing – culturally, politically, and personally? In her powerful new book, How to Kill a Language, award-winning author and journalist Sophia Smith Galer journeys across continents and generations to ask this crucial question. Today, she’s joined by iconic Scots poet Len Pennie, author of the defiant Poyums Annaw, to explore bilingual identity, the erasure of languages, and the efforts being made to revitalise them. Chaired by Beth Cochrane.

events.title: Gavin Francis: The Unfragile Mind
events.blurb: Between 30-50% of GP consultations now concern mental health. As a GP for over 20 years, Gavin Francis has had a front row seat to society’s changing ideas of mental illness. The Unfragile Mind draws on hundreds of conversations with patients and specialist colleagues about mental suffering and how best to ease it. With Karine Polwart today, he argues that society’s current approach is overly rigid, and would benefit from more curiosity, humility, kindness, and hope.

events.title: A Birthday Party for… Winnie the Pooh
events.blurb: Mark your calendars, dust off your dancing shoes, and get ready to party! Loads of our favourite books have big anniversaries this year so we’re throwing some of them a special birthday bash. Come along today to celebrate Winnie the Pooh, A A Milne’s beloved children’s classic that’s now a giant 100 years old! There’ll be storytime, party games, dancing, and singing as we wish our favourite silly old bear many happy returns.

events.title: Mark Haddon: Leaving Home
events.blurb: As an artist and multi-million copy bestselling writer, Mark Haddon is known for constructing vivid worlds through his imagery and storytelling. Now, he reflects on his own world with Leaving Home: his richly illustrated and darkly hilarious memoir about growing up in the East Midlands. In this fascinating conversation, the Booker-longlisted author of The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-time talks family, art, and what it means to see the world differently. Chaired by Rodge Glass.

events.title: Baby Animals are the Best with Holly Webb
events.blurb: If you adore animals – especially fluffy ones – here’s a warm and cuddly event for you. Author Holly Webb is here to chat about how she researches her animal-themed stories, and she’s got lots of baby animal pictures to show you! Hear all about The Proud Puppy, and what inspired her to write about Emmie and her adorable puppy Loki as they get ready for her uncle's wedding.

events.title: Have Lunch with Ben Lippett
events.blurb: Amassing a million-strong following with his warm, funny videos on how to nail ‘cheffy’ recipes like sausage and sage pappardelle, Ben Lippett makes the kitchen the coolest place to be. Today he’ll draw on his instant bestseller How I Cook to serve lunch with a side of practical advice on preparing restaurant-quality food, no matter your skill level. Ticket includes: a welcome drink, a generous multi-course lunch, and paired wine on the table.

events.title: Writing for Children: A Workshop with Catherine Coe, Patrice Lawrence & Rashmi Sirdeshpande
events.blurb: Have you always wanted to write for children but don’t know where to start? Keen to understand your characters, plot, and audience better? This friendly, illuminating workshop with award-winning authors Patrice Lawrence and Rashmi Sirdeshpande will leave you encouraged, inspired, and raring to go. Plus, discover more about All Stories, a charity founded by Catharine Coe to support underrepresented children’s book writers. See website for details on subsidised virtual places for participants from low-income backgrounds.

events.title: Come on a Catwalk with Karen Mabon
events.blurb: Love fashion? Love cats? Here’s the purrrrfect event for you! Come on a fabulous global adventure with Scottish designer Karen Mabon and her new book, A Catwalk Around the World. Hang out with the best-dressed cats you’ve ever met and discover incredible things about our world through fashions in Paris, China, and beyond – then get crafty with a fashionably fun activity. It’s going to be un-fur-gettable!

events.title: Tom Newlands: Something Like Happiness
events.blurb: There’s an unmistakable buzz around Tom Newlands. Winner of Waterstones’ 2025 Scottish Book of the Year with his debut, Only Here, Only Now, his blistering second novel, Something Like Happiness, follows Frazer and Caitlin from puppy love to impoverished parenthood in a story shot through with humour and poignancy. Definitely a talent to watch, join Newlands to reflect on whether love is enough when the world has stacked the odds against you. Chaired by Beth Cochrane.

events.title: Animal Magic with Catherine Rayner
events.blurb: If you can’t get enough of animals and art, get your tickets quick! Beloved author-illustrator Catherine Rayner will show you how she makes her beautiful beasts spring off the page. No one captures an animal’s expression, personality, and movement quite like Catherine – just look at Augustus and his Smile! This friendly session will encourage everyone to believe in their own drawing, writing, and creativity as Catherine shares her brand new book.

events.title: Meet the Gruffalo
events.blurb: Oh help! Oh no! It’s the Gruffalo! But don’t worry, he’s incredibly friendly and can’t wait to meet you! Come along for a photo and a cuddle while he’s visiting from the deep dark wood.

events.title: Yi-Ling Liu: The Wall Dancers
events.blurb: If all the web users in China formed their own country, it would be Earth’s third most populous… yet the wider world has little idea of what goes on behind the Great Firewall. Today, journalist Yi-Ling Liu discusses her new book, The Wall Dancers – a revealing look at China’s internet; not just the censorship and surveillance that exist, but also the abundant memes, subcultures, and activisms which challenge our assumptions about Chinese digital society. Chaired by Jenny Niven.

events.title: Ask Philippa – Live
events.blurb: Sometimes we need a helping hand to untie life’s trickier knots, be it falling out with a close friend or a messy situationship. Fear not: the nation’s favourite therapist Philippa Perry is here to play agony aunt in a live version of her beloved Ask Philippa column, formerly of the Guardian and now on Substack. From romantic dilemmas to workplace woes, there’s no problem too big (or small). Submit your questions via askphilippa@edbookfest.co.uk. Chaired by Simon Preston.

events.title: Meet the Gruffalo
events.blurb: Oh help! Oh no! It’s the Gruffalo! But don’t worry, he’s incredibly friendly and can’t wait to meet you! Come along for a photo and a cuddle while he’s visiting from the deep dark wood.

events.title: Write Your Own Animal Story with Holly Webb
events.blurb: Are you bursting with ideas for your own animal story? Well, brilliant animal-story expert Holly Webb will help you write it! Come along to Holly’s super-friendly session and get scribbling. See what characters, plots, and animal adventures pop out of your head. Pets, porcupines, pterodactyls? Everyone’s welcome at this playful event. No experience or materials needed – just bring your imagination!

events.title: Brodie Crellin and Susannah Dickey: Under One Roof
events.blurb: Death brings people together, right? For the families at the heart of Brodie Crellin’s A Sense of Occasion and Susannah Dickey’s Into the Wreck, things aren’t so simple. Reunited under one roof, the characters in these sharp, witty novels must navigate their grief, coming together while laying bare old wounds. Join Dickey and Crellin in conversation as they talk about loss, atonement, and what makes families tick. Chaired by Caoilinn Hughes.

events.title: Oyinkan Braithwaite: Cursed Daughters
events.blurb: Oyinkan Braithwaite’s Booker Prize-longlisted debut, My Sister, The Serial Killer, swiftly became a viral publishing sensation. Her hotly anticipated second novel, Cursed Daughters, is a deliciously dark tale about a family curse, reincarnation, female rivalry, and haunting secrets. Join Braithwaite to explore the strength of familial beliefs, taking a risk on love, and the powerful forces which can be unleashed if we try to swerve grief. Chaired by Carmen Thompson.

events.title: Loud Poets Grand Slam Final
events.blurb: Back again for another year of electrifying slam poetry, this heated competition from Loud Poets gives new meaning to the phrase ‘poetry in motion’. Having qualified through a series of nationwide Slams, 10 poets compete for a cash prize, glory, and the coveted title of Slam Champion. Host Kevin Mclean brings you along for the final showdown in an event that promises to deliver a poetic knockout. Aditya Narayan joins this event as the Sacrificial Poet.

events.title: Orlando Swayne: How to Use a Fork
events.blurb: A consultant neurologist with a particular interest in neurorehabilitation, Orlando Swayne’s work has taught him that a brain that’s been ‘broken’ has the potential to form new connections and mend itself. Speaking profoundly to our Changing Your Mind theme, Swayne discusses How to Use a Fork: Stories of Mending the Broken Brain: his fascinating exploration of human recovery and survival that brings real-world rehabilitation case studies to life, asking questions about the very nature of consciousness itself. Chaired by Maddison Connaughton.

events.title: Meet the Gruffalo
events.blurb: Oh help! Oh no! It’s the Gruffalo! But don’t worry, he’s incredibly friendly and can’t wait to meet you! Come along for a photo and a cuddle while he’s visiting from the deep dark wood.

events.title: Catherine Opie, Del LaGrace Volcano & Gemma Rolls-Bentley: Radical Imagery
events.blurb: This year, EAF (Edinburgh Art Festival) welcomes the radical work of two cult American photographers: Catherine Opie and Del LaGrace Volcano. Volcano’s Love Bites Back is an exhibition of dyke photography, while Opie’s To Be Seen features nearly 80 portraits of those commonly missing from mainstream art history. Both pioneering photographers, they join Kim McAleese, director of EAF, to speak about their work and their portrayal of often invisible communities. Gemma Rolls-Bentley will be participating in this event.

events.title: So Many Feelings with Nat Luurtsema and Rashmi Sirdeshpande
events.blurb: If you’ve ever had worries, friends, dreams, or felt, like, any feelings ever… this one’s for you. Nat Luurtsema’s The Overthinkers Club follows Birdie who’s dealing with A LOT and making a Happy List to cheer herself up. Rashmi Sirdeshpande’s Hari Kumar follows Hari, who dreams of victory… if things would just go to plan. Hear two very funny writers chat about how comedy and feelings make the perfect book recipe. Chaired by Eleanor Morton.

events.title: Amber Husain & Rebecca May Johnson: Eating Their Words (AMBER HUSAIN IS APPEARING REMOTELY)
events.blurb: Why are domestic kitchens deemed ‘women’s spaces’ while most Michelin-starred chefs are men? What does it mean to follow your appetite, remix recipes, and reject food as ‘good’ or ‘bad’? Today, Amber Husain and Rebecca May Johnson discuss piercing questions around food, politics, and gender in Tell Me How You Eat and Small Fires: one a deeply personal exploration of anorexia and the politics of eating, the other a manifesto for cooking as an intellectual act. Chaired by Ali Millar.

events.title: Peter Apps & Lina Khatib: The Next World War
events.blurb: It would be easy to say that for the first time since the Cold War, the next world war feels like a matter of ‘when’, not ‘if’. Here to give us clear, cool-headed insight into where the world might be going are Lina Khatib, Associate Fellow at Chatham House’s Middle East and North Africa Programme, and Reuters defence correspondent Peter Apps, whose The Next World War gives an insider account of preparations to combat the new ‘axis of upheaval’. Chaired by Jo Sharp.

events.title: Ashley Douglas, Kate Lister & Jean Menzies: Ladies of Pleasure
events.blurb: Women’s sexuality is often missing from the history books, but reading between the lines can reveal a lot about how female pleasure has been controlled, misunderstood, and set free over the centuries. Today, the Festival brings together three writers who’ve been thinking deeply about the role of sex in women’s stories: Flick author Kate Lister, Aphrodisia author Jean Menzies, and Ashley Douglas, the historian uncovering Scotland’s 16th-century Sappho in With My Own Hand. Chaired by Vic Murray.

events.title: Emma-Lee Moss: My Cantopop Nights
events.blurb: Singer-songwriter Emma-Lee Moss, AKA Emmy the Great, reflects with Katie Goh on her personal journey through music, fandom, and identity (and performs a few songs for us too). My Cantopop Nights explores the stars Moss idolised throughout her Hong Kong upbringing and the subsequent loss of identity when her family moved to England. Hear her trace how this hidden passion intertwined with Hong Kong’s post-colonial tensions, becoming both a refuge and a symbol of her childhood self.

events.title: Your Voice Matters with Manjeet Mann
events.blurb: What does it mean to find your voice? What would it mean to ROAR with it? Get inspired as award-winning author and performer Manjeet Mann shares the real-life story behind Roar: her bold new verse novel of resistance, based on the activism of Sampat Pal and the Pink Sari Gang. Discover how Manjeet first got into writing and the experiences that have shaped her, then tap into your own courage to create a fresh new work.

events.title: Daisy Johnson & Doireann Ní Ghríofa: Kindred Spirits
events.blurb: Mixing archive and memory, Doireann Ní Ghríofa’s Said the Dead draws readers into a haunting illumination of Cork’s forgotten women. In Daisy Johnson’s hypnotic Long Wave, a foundling discovered on an island contends with new motherhood while, years earlier, a pregnant woman, locked away by her own mother, dreams of escape. These visionary writers join us to discuss memory, whispers from the past, and the stories that survive us. Chaired by Niamh Ní Mhaoileoin.

events.title: Opening Night Gala
events.blurb:
Celebrate the opening of this year’s Festival in this captivating evening of new, specially commissioned writing, hosted by Festival director, Jenny Niven. We’ll bring you a kaleidoscope of perspectives and provocations from a diverse line-up of stellar writers, including Y M Abdel-Magied, Graeme Armstrong, Anne Enright, Gavin Francis, Naomi Ishiguro, and Jackie Kay, as they each read powerful new pieces of writing responding to our 2026 theme of Changing Your Mind, with music from Aidan O’Rourke. Harben Kay joins this line-up as a musical guest.

Check back soon for the full line-up.

events.title: Relaxed Screening: Beano: The Funniest Dennis the Menace story EVER!
events.blurb: Some of us thrive better in smaller, informal spaces. That’s why we’re putting on this relaxed screening for anyone with sensory sensitivities. You can watch the livestream of Beano: Lost in Time with Craig Graham & Mike Stirling while being able to move around, come and go, and make noise in this friendly, chilled out space.

events.title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
events.blurb: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers with Jill Calder.

events.title: Music and Mayhem with Dougie Payne & Rachel Seago
events.blurb: Lonely, scruffy, and hopelessly clumsy, Pete’s feet have always got him in trouble – until he stumbles into a music shop and finds his place in the world. Discover Poochie Pete and his Very Big Feet, a radiant rhyming tale written by Dougie Payne (who grown-ups might know from Glasgow band, Travis) and illustrated by Rachel Seago, in this event full of heart, song, stories, and drawing.

events.title: Beano: The Funniest Dennis the Menace story EVER!
events.blurb: Dennis the Menace has a special birthday wish – he wants to break the rules of reading! Beano’s Directors of Mischief and Mayhem, Mike Stirling and Craig Graham, help him, revealing their top-secret tips for creating the laugh-out-loud stories and comic strips in Beano, where Dennis has starred since 1951. PLUS they reveal insider info on how they’ve reinvented reading with their smash-hit latest Beano Boomic Dennis the Menace: Mischief at the Museum. Join their Mischief Squad, as you help co-create the funniest Dennis the Menace comic strip of ALL-TIME! It's the cheekiest, funniest, most creative show ever!

events.title: The More You Know with the National Museum of Scotland
events.blurb: How does a cyclops become a mammoth, or a tiger become a cat? Come and find out in this drop-in session with our brilliant pals from the National Museum of Scotland. Get hands-on and find out how we’re always learning new things about the past, then discover more about the prehistoric animals in the Museum’s Giants exhibition and what on earth it means to be a palaeontologist!

events.title: Patrick Gale & Lisa Ridzén: Before It’s Too Late
events.blurb: Family frailty and how ageing fathers ache for connection as the clock ticks down: these are the threads linking Patrick Gale’s Love Lane (the follow-up to his Costa Novel Prize-shortlisted A Place Called Winter) and Lisa Ridzén’s heartrending debut, When the Cranes Fly South. Is it ever too late for reconciliation? Brace your nerve endings for a powerful conversation between the authors as they reflect on regret, forgiveness, and their profoundly life-affirming novels. Chaired by Nicole Abadee.

events.title: Chopping and Changing: A Poetry Workshop with Peter Mackay
events.blurb: National Makar Peter Mackay knows that words come to us slightly battered and dented. What do we do with these imperfect tools? How do we put them together in meaningful, powerful ways? How do we harness their ‘usedness’ to change what our minds might say? In this poetry workshop, explore different means of changing our (and others’) minds, re-envisioning words and images, deciding what’s for the chop, and what can be repurposed to create new, imaginary worlds.

events.title: Eating and Waiting to Eat: Podcast Live – with Ben Lippett
events.blurb: Two Americans walk into a bakery and leave with a podcast. Not the start of a joke, but the origin story of Kevin Rivers and Carlos Miranda’s beloved, Edinburgh-based Eating and Waiting to Eat podcast. In this live episode, the pair chat about the hows and whys behind everything we do in the kitchen with professional-chef-turned-home-cook Ben Lippett, whose stunning debut, How I Cook, is celebrated by the likes of Nigella Lawson and Yotam Ottolenghi.

events.title: Reimagining Fairy Tales with Craigmillar Literacy Trust
events.blurb: Join Katie Swann from Craigmillar Literacy Trust for a magical, hands-on event all about your favourite fairytales from around the world – but maybe not quite as you remember them. Katie will share a selection of stunning picture books, then show you how to make a simple puppet theatre show to share your own stories at home. Kids and their grown-ups are welcome to explore, learn, and get creative together. See you there!

events.title: Rachel Aviv & Catherine Carr: It’s All Relative
events.blurb: Two skilled storytellers meet to mine the rich vein of family dynamics. In You Won’t Get Free of It, The New Yorker journalist Rachel Aviv collects real stories of mothers and daughters to intimate and revelatory effect, while documentarian Catherine Carr’s Who’s the Favourite? puts the messy reality of adult siblinghood under the microscope. Leave confronted, comforted, and filled with food for thought about your most formative relationships and place in the family. Chaired by Caoilinn Hughes.

events.title: Sparkling Creativity with Harriet Muncaster
events.blurb: Woohoo, our favourite half-vampire half-fairy Isadora Moon is 10 years old! Join the celebrations with Harriet Muncaster and her magical book, Isadora Moon Has a Birthday. Along with spellbinding interactive and creative activities, Harriet will read adorable tales about Isadora and Pink Rabbit, and also share her brand-new book, The Diary of Wiska Wildflower: The New School. Let's chat about friendship, courage, and life changes in the sweetest, sparkliest way possible.

events.title: A Birthday Party for… Pip and Posy
events.blurb: Mark your calendars, dust off your dancing shoes, and get ready to party! Loads of our favourite books have big anniversaries this year so we’re throwing some of them a special birthday bash. Come along today to celebrate the 15th anniversary of the Pip and Posy series by Camilla Reid and Axel Scheffler. There’ll be storytime, party games, dancing, and singing as we wish our favourite animal pals many happy returns.

events.title: Vote For a Laugh with Nadia Shireen
events.blurb: Fancy a bit of woodland wackiness? You’ve come to the right place! Drop in on the latest goings-on in the Grimwood series, with its hilarious creator Nadia Shireen. You can bet she’ll have you laughing your socks off as she shares her latest story, Grimwood: Rock the Vote. This time, the loveably loopy animals are choosing a new mayor… but who’s got what it takes? A warm and interactive event filled with animal antics.

events.title: Jill Dawson: Pixie
events.blurb: Thousands consult Tarot cards about the paths they should be taking, but few know the name of Pamela ‘Pixie’ Colman Smith, illustrator of the world’s most iconic Tarot deck. In fictionalised biography Pixie, her life as a plucky fin-de-siècle artist drawn to the occult is conjured up by Orange Prize-shortlisted author Jill Dawson. A qualified Jungian Tarot reader herself, if you bring your dilemmas today, Dawson might just show you the way. Chaired by Kirsty Logan.

events.title: Have Lunch with Gurdeep Loyal
events.blurb: Have you tried spicy harissa lasagne? Or added sesame oil to a sundae? In Flavour Heroes, Gurdeep Loyal combines his expertise as a food and travel writer to dissolve the imaginary borders around culinary cultures. Join him at the table as he prepares a flavour-rich, globe-trotting meal that will get your synapses (and tastebuds) firing on all cylinders. Ticket includes: a welcome drink, a generous multi-course lunch, and paired wine on the table.

events.title: A Freshly-Baked Mystery with Harry Woodgate
events.blurb: When rival bakers Victoria Sponge and Madeleine Macaroon cook up wicked ways to win the Great Cake Carnival, it’s time for local girl Cinnamon Crumb to turn detective. In Harry Woodgate’s delectable new chapter book, Cinnamon Crumb, Baking Detective: The Great Cake Caper, plots rise and sabotage spreads. So come and grab a taste of Harry’s yummy new series and roll up your sleeves for a delicious group activity.

events.title: Charlotte McConaghy: Wild Dark Shore
events.blurb: What does it mean to raise children in an ecological crisis? New York Times bestselling author Charlotte McConaghy felt the weight of this question while pregnant – and that’s how Wild Dark Shore came into the world. An eco-thriller set on a storm-lashed island, the novel (longlisted for 2026’s Women’s Prize for Fiction) vibrates with eerie beauty. Today the author discusses courage and how far we might go for the people, and wildernesses, we love. Chaired by David Farrier.

events.title: Philippa Perry: Shrink Solves Murder
events.blurb: When a man’s body washes up near Beachy Head, the police call it suicide – but his therapist is not convinced. Shrink Solves Murder is a cosy crime caper so deft in its unpicking of the human condition that you’ll wonder why Philippa Perry didn’t pour her expertise into novel-writing sooner. Don’t miss the beloved psychotherapist, agony aunt, and bestselling author of The Book You Wish Your Parents Had Read, in conversation with Sam Baker today. This event is chaired by Zara Janjua.

events.title: Meet Pip and Posy
events.blurb: Our favourite mouse and rabbit BFFs are back! Pip and Posy would love to say hello and introduce you to their brilliant new trail around the Children’s Tent. Pose for a photo, cosy in for a cuddle, or give them a high-five – come and hang out with the kindest animals in town.

events.title: Beeban Kidron & Sarah Wynn-Williams: Safety in an Online World?
events.blurb: Leading online safety campaigner, legislator, and filmmaker Baroness Beeban Kidron reveals how unchecked tech giants are exploiting young minds in both her acclaimed 2013 documentary, InRealLife, and new book, Users: How Big Tech Took Control and How to Fight Back. Today, Kidron joins us to unpack how we might fight back and protect the next generations from online harms. Also featuring Sarah Wynn-Williams. Check back soon for full details. Chaired by Catriona Stewart.

events.title: Sounding Home: A Songwriting Workshop with Emma-Lee Moss
events.blurb: How do we remember where we’ve been? Which songs help shape and preserve our identities? This playful session – led by musician and My Cantopop Nights author Emma-Lee Moss (AKA Emmy the Great) – invites you to explore gentle creative exercises, share the songs that remind you of home, and write about your own special places. Together, you’ll build a communal song that weaves a collective dream of a shared world. Open to all experience levels. Instruments welcome, though not required.

events.title: Jay Gao & Karen McCarthy Woolf: Embodied Natures
events.blurb: Two poets turn their singular attention to the human body’s relationship with nature. In Jay Gao’s The Dead One, trees become portals to a dream world of haunting and memory. Join Gao and McCarthy Woolf to discuss the role poetry might play in re-sensitising us to the living world. Chaired by Samuel Tongue.

events.title: Famous Fun & Games with Little People, BIG DREAMS
events.blurb: Calling all BIG DREAMERS! Fancy taking part in a gameshow that’s all about believing in yourself? Come and celebrate 10 years of Little People BIG DREAMS, the books that show you how famous people believed in their true selves and made a difference. Meet series author Maria Isabel Sánchez Vegara, illustrator Sara Rhys and musicians Dom James and Tommy Antonio (who'll be playing music from the new Little People, BIG DREAMS album!) Featuring rounds of singalongs, quizzes, drawing and much more, all hosted by comedian Athena Kugblenu, this is an event that teaches courage and self-confidence are what it’s all about!

events.title: Meet Pip and Posy
events.blurb: Our favourite mouse and rabbit BFFs are back! Pip and Posy would love to say hello and introduce you to their brilliant new trail around the Children’s Tent. Pose for a photo, cosy in for a cuddle, or give them a high-five – come and hang out with the kindest animals in town.

events.title: Shadow School with Peter Burns
events.blurb: Reckon you’ve got what it takes to make it as a professional thief at Beaufort’s School for Deceptive Arts? Join author Peter Burns, who’ll test whether you’re ready for the Shadow League. He’ll introduce you to the mysterious world of his series, Shadow Thieves, featuring plucky orphan Tom, whose survival skills are put to the test when he must battle the great villain, the Duke of Nimes. Would your street smarts be up to the task?

events.title: Naomi Ishiguro & Katalina Watt: High-Octane Folklore
events.blurb: If fast-paced fantasy plots are your thing, secure your seat for Naomi Ishiguro and Katalina Watt. In The Rainshadow Orphans, Ishiguro draws on Japanese folklore and Studio Ghibli to tell a story of righteous revenge, while Watt’s Saltswept takes you on a perilous quest through Southeast Asian mythology in search of hidden treasure. Join them for a fascinating chat about magical histories and why the world's oldest stories still have so much to teach us. Chaired by Kirsty Logan.

events.title: Cory Doctorow: Enshittification
events.blurb: Tech critic, sci-fi author, and seer of digital dystopia, Cory Doctorow’s Enshittification: Why Everything Suddenly Got Worse and What to Do About It is a blistering take-down of formerly utopian tech companies’ constant chase for bigger profits. In this urgent discussion with Heather Parry, Doctorow sets out the case for how to cure ourselves from the lure of big tech, resist the monetisation of every aspect of our lives, demand regulation, and reclaim our privacy online.

events.title: When Rights Collide
events.blurb: How can we use the law as a framework to protect the rights of all? Today’s event, featuring a panel of legal experts, explores the Supreme Court’s recent ruling on the legal definition of a woman and what it means in practice. Can previous cases where rights have appeared to be in competition help illuminate a pathway forward? We invite audience members for a good faith discussion on this contested and challenging topic, with the aim of achieving better understanding and more empathy. With Baroness Brenda Hale, Karon Monaghan KC, and Keio Yoshida. Chaired by Catriona Stewart.

events.title: Word Salad
events.blurb: Hungry for some hearty food chat? Peter Simpson, editor of The Skinny’s food magazine GNAW, hosts a spirited round table with Times restaurant critic Chitra Ramaswamy, founder of Fare magazine Ben Mervis, and Rebecca May Johnson, editor at Vittles and author of Small Fires. From reviews to long-form explorations of food culture, memoirs to memes and mailouts, they'll discuss the ever-expanding ways that writers share their thoughts on what we eat, and why.

events.title: Zoulfa Katouh: The Ocean Would Paint Me Blue
events.blurb: How do you start from scratch when grief looms large? In The Ocean Would Paint Me Blue, Zoulfa Katouh tells the story of Jihad, a young woman navigating a prestigious new school as the only Muslim student there. The internationally bestselling author of As Long as the Lemon Trees Grow joins the Festival for a chat about friendship, resilience, and identity – we’d love for  you to be part of the conversation too.

events.title: History’s Most Epic Fails with Athena Kugblenu
events.blurb: History’s full of daring deeds, mighty heroes, and incredible inventions. But it’s also full of huge FAILS! Discover the truths behind the world’s biggest howlers with comedian and CBBC Horrible Histories writer, Athena Kugblenu, author of History’s Most Epic Fails. Whether it’s silly mishaps that changed the course of history or mistakes that did us all a favour, Athena will take you on a riotous ride through the past.

events.title: Tarot for Fiction Writers: A Workshop with Jill Dawson
events.blurb: While writing her novel Fred and Edie, Jill Dawson was stuck and decided, as a writing exercise, to give the book’s protagonist a tarot reading. 26 years later, and now a qualified Jungian Tarot reader, Dawson has used tarot to develop her writing in many ways since. Join her for this interactive workshop exploring using the tarot to overcome creative blocks, unlock voice and form, solve narrative puzzles, and expand your writing practice. No experience of tarot needed!

events.title: Big Tech (and What to Do About It): A Changing Ideas Workshop
events.blurb: Do you deeply feel the urgency of the challenges that face us, but don’t know how to channel that into meaningful action? Designed as a follow-on for attendees of ‘Safety in an Online World’, this workshop – co-created with Changing Ideas and facilitated by Civic Digits’ artistic director Clare Duffy – aims to help bridge that gap. Join our action-focussed discussion on online safety and leave feeling empowered to take practical next steps.

events.title: Jess Kidd: Modern Gothic (ESSIE FOX HAS CANCELLED)
events.blurb: Catherine Earnshaw rises from the grave to set the record straight. An orphan with electricity in her fingertips is sent to a house where inventors build living machines. Essie Fox's Catherine reimagines Brontë’s Wuthering Heights while Jess Kidd's Little Spark blends gothic with steampunk to spellbinding effect. Together, the 'Queen of Victoriana' and the bestselling author of Things in Jars discuss atmosphere, secrets, and why gothic still grips us with Beth Cochrane.

events.title: Irvine Welsh: Can Nothing Save Us?
events.blurb: Scotland’s grittiest writer returns to launch Can Nothing Save Us? – a ferocious saga of moral freefall, set in a blisteringly hot Las Vegas. Irvine Welsh turns his unflinching gaze on a nation in crisis with this novel following three generations of a wealthy, divided family spiralling toward paranoia, drug-fuelled excess, and explosive reckoning. Join the bard of bad behaviour – 30 years on from the Trainspotting movie – for an unfiltered chat about power, entitlement, and moral decay with Kevin Williamson.

events.title: Rachel Aviv: Strangers to Ourselves
events.blurb: Join long-time New Yorker journalist Rachel Aviv, renowned for her in-depth reporting on topics ranging from police shootings in Albuquerque to the complex case of neonatal nurse Lucy Letby. Strangers to Ourselves, centred around five people’s psychiatric testimonies and Aviv’s own childhood, explores how society and storytelling shape our experience of mental illness. A remarkable book, it treats the human mind with the subtlety, complexity, and care it deserves. Chaired by Maddison Connaughton.

events.title: Our Many-Voiced Country
events.blurb: Now in his second year as Makar, Peter Mackay brings together contemporary poets working in Scotland who showcase the range of languages being spoken and written across the country. From English, Catalan, Orcadian, Scots and Gaelic, to Tamil, Arabic, Persian, and Kutchi (and beyond!), this special event will weave together a tapestry of multi-language poetry, featuring performances from: Helena Fornells Nadal, Harry Josephine Giles, Marjorie Lotfi, Robbie Macleòid, Q Mannivanan, and Alycia Pirmohamed.

events.title: qntm: There Is No Antimemetics Division
events.blurb: An antimeme is an idea you can't hold onto – a dream, a dirty secret, a complex equation. Now imagine one that's hunting you. Software engineer turned cult literary sensation qntm joins us with There Is No Antimemetics Division: a mind-bending debut blending cosmic horror with jaw-dropping ideas that asks what happens when reality itself becomes unreliable. One of the Guardian's best sci-fi books of 2025, this is unlike anything you've read. Chaired by Russell Jones.

events.title: Annie Lord & Elle McNicoll: Love, or Something Like It [BOBBY PALMER is no longer participating]
events.blurb: Packed with stories that take on love in unconventional ways, contemporary romance has got hot again. Just ask Vogue columnist Annie Lord (The Project), beloved YA author turned debut adult novelist Elle McNicoll (Unapologetic Love Story), and bestselling author and journalist Bobby Palmer (Main Characters) – all of whose novels explore modern relationships, intimacy, and life-changing connections. The trio gathers for an uplifting chat about love stories for the 21st century, and why we still believe. Chaired by Nyla Ahmad.

events.title: Abir Mukherjee: The Pinnacle
events.blurb: Welcome to the Pinnacle, Mumbai’s grandest skyscraper, where privilege lives high above desperation, and every floor has its secrets. In his most propulsive thriller yet, Abir Mukherjee’s The Pinnacle follows a washed-up Hollywood actor accused of killing his Bollywood-superstar wife. Did he do it? The bestselling author of Hunted and the Wyndham & Banerjee series joins us to talk glamour, celebrity, satire, and the view from the very top. Chaired by Kim Sherwood.

events.title: India Alba & William Dalrymple: The Golden Road
events.blurb:
Historian William Dalrymple is renowned for his decades of research about India’s pivotal role in shaping the ancient world, and for uncovering connections between the past and present. This  special event – fresh from Celtic Connections – includes readings from Dalrymple about the history and relationship between India and Scotland, as well as music from the astounding India Alba collective, who fuse the raga gats of Indian classical music with the melodies of the Scottish Highlands.

Part of Scotland to the World. Supported by Sir Ewan and Lady Brown and The Consulate General of India, Edinburgh.

events.title: Rob Drummond, Dave Hook & Orla O’Loughlin: Hip-Hop Wallace
events.blurb: An exhilarating collision of Scottish rap and historical mythmaking, Wallace: A Musical is a playful, humour-filled retelling of the story of William Wallace that packs a punch. Join playwright Rob Drummond, director Orla O’Loughlin, and rapper Dave Hook as they talk about what it takes to reinvent a national legend. And in a Festival first, audiences will be treated to a delicious live sample of the show itself, before it heads on tour this autumn. Manasa Tagica and Patricia Panther are now joining this event.

events.title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
events.blurb: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Check website for today's author.

events.title: Pop in and Play
events.blurb: Come and play with us! Everyone is welcome for our 30-minute guided sessions of fun and games, ideal to keep your wee ones busy. We know that great stories can come from great playtimes (no matter your age) so on your marks… get set… imagine!

events.title: Andrea Wulf: The Traveller
events.blurb: Step into the shoes of the most consequential man you’ve maybe never heard of. Award-winning historian Andrea Wulf talks to Fiammetta Rocco about The Traveller: The Revolutionary Life of George Forster and his Search for Humanity, recounting the young naturalist who journeyed to the far reaches of the known world on Captain Cook’s second voyage. A visionary proto-activist, his travels inspired radical ideas about humanity, equality, and freedom at odds with the worldviews of his time.

events.title: Shared Reading with Open Book
events.blurb: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session. Each session will explore a chapter from a debut book from this year’s Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading materials will be provided on the day.

events.title: Frank Cottrell-Boyce: A British Childhood
events.blurb: What does it mean to be young in Britain today? As Waterstones Children’s Laureate, Frank Cottrell-Boyce has met children from many – often precarious – backgrounds, and A British Childhood is his piercing examination of how community, and connection, are fraying. This urgent conversation sees the inaugural Children’s Booker Prize chair sharing illuminating, real stories from Britain’s homes, schools, and streets – and a message of hope too. Chaired by Noëlle Cobden.

events.title: Confetti with Dean Atta
events.blurb: This event has been specially designed for our visitors with learning disabilities, including PMLD. Dean Atta will lead an event full of sensory moments in a gently playful telling of his delightful picture book, Confetti. Doors will open early so you can get yourself settled in, and additional staff will be on hand to make sure everyone feels comfortable and welcome.

events.title: Aonghus MacKechnie: City of Romanticism
events.blurb: A castellated, stone city draped over a dramatic landscape – travellers have been drawn to the romantic beauty of Edinburgh’s architecture for centuries. In his new book, Edinburgh: City of Romanticism, historian Aonghus MacKechnie reveals how our capital developed as a hub for writers, poets, artists, and musicians, through the lens of its emblematic architecture that still attracts over four million tourists every year. A conversation for anyone in love with art, architecture, and Edinburgh itself. Chaired by Gabriella Bennett.

events.title: Pop in and Play
events.blurb: Come and play with us! Everyone is welcome for our 30-minute guided sessions of fun and games, ideal to keep your wee ones busy. We know that great stories can come from great playtimes (no matter your age) so on your marks… get set… imagine!

events.title: How Can We Build a Feminist Scotland?
events.blurb:
In Building a Feminist Nation, social justice campaigner Talat Yaqoob, modern historian Helen O’Shea, and Law professor Kim Barker commissioned bold new writing on the intersection of feminism, human rights, advocacy, and policy to prompt vital discussions about
Scotland. Esa Aldegheri talks with them and contributors Muminah Koleoso (writing on young women and misogyny) and Catherine Murphy (exploring poverty and the economy), considering the political shifts required to deliver a more equitable, feminist Scotland.

events.title: Brenda Hale: With the Law on Our Side
events.blurb: Baroness Brenda Hale of Richmond was the first woman to serve as President of the Supreme Court of the United Kingdom. With decades of experience as a judge and an intimate knowledge of British law, her new book, With the Law on Our Side – longlisted for 2026’s Women’s Prize for Non-Fiction – uses true stories to explore the complexities of real court decisions. Join Lady Hale to learn how the law works, why we should care about it, and how it can be used to protect all of our rights. Chaired by Claire Mitchell.

events.title: The Front List: Cory Doctorow and Jimmy Wales
events.blurb: Remember when the internet was exciting and full of possibilities? As online content becomes darker, more divisive, and sensationalist over truthful, join Jimmy Wales, founder of Wikipedia and author of The Seven Rules of Trust, and journalist and sci-fi author Cory Doctorow (author of Enshittification: Why Everything Suddenly Got Worse and What To Do About It) for a frank and fascinating discussion on the current state of our online lives. Can the internet ever be good again?

events.title: Everybody Dance! with Mariko Miyata Jancey
events.blurb: Mariko Miyata Jancey loves to dance…and she’d love it if you danced too! Coming on a special trip from Norway, she’s bringing her beautiful picture book Mieko Danser which is all about being just who you are… and having a brilliant boogie while you’re at it. With dancing, music, and lots of happiness, this is a rare chance to see an incredible writer and performer in action.

events.title: Tariq Ashkanani & Kirsty Lockwood: Breaking the Silence
events.blurb: Tariq Ashkanani, winner of the McIlvanney Prize 2025, presents his latest thriller, The Hollow Boys, following a young boy’s return 10 months after disappearing. Meanwhile, Scottish political journalist Kirsty Lockwood introduces her debut, We Know What You Did, in which a seemingly sweet, lonely girl refuses to speak following a livestreamed murder. Today, both crime novelists join Bryan Burnett to talk murder, mystery, and menace.

events.title: Close Read: Wuthering Heights by Emily Brontë
events.blurb: In our Close Read series, a brilliant author guides you through a deep-diving discussion of a classic text or genre that’s inspired them. Think of it as an event blending friendly book club vibes with insightful study notes. Today, Sunday Times bestseller Essie Fox (author of Catherine: A Retelling of Wuthering Heights) shares her deep understanding of Emily Brontë’s seminal gothic novel. With Fox’s insight, uncover the many layers of love, tumult, and wild landscapes.

events.title: Edward Fishman: How Economic Warfare is Changing the World
events.blurb: The global oil market follows critical arteries, and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is a demonstration of the fragility of the system; a block at any one point has far-reaching effects, and global influence can be wielded through disruption. Leading authority on economic statecraft and sanctions, Edward Fishman joins us today to discuss Chokepoints, offering a timely illumination of modern economic warfare in the age of globalisation. Chaired by Mure Dickie.

events.title: Pop in and Play
events.blurb: Come and play with us! Everyone is welcome for our 30-minute guided sessions of fun and games, ideal to keep your wee ones busy. We know that great stories can come from great playtimes (no matter your age) so on your marks… get set… imagine!

events.title: The Front List: Val McDermid & Jo Sharp
events.blurb: Did you know that in the 17th century, Scotland tried to establish a colonial project in Panama? Hear acclaimed crime novelist Val McDermid and Geographer Royal for Scotland Jo Sharp chat with Allan Little about their fictional retelling of this surprising story from our country’s history. This Door of the Seas, framed through letters home, reveals Scotland’s colonial ambitions and how they ultimately failed, bankrupting the nation and setting Scotland on a path towards union with England.

events.title: Janina Ramirez: Legenda
events.blurb: Cultural historian Janina Ramirez is turning history on its head again. Following the success of Femina – her instant bestseller exploring the Middle Ages through the women written out of it – her latest book, Legenda, looks at the flesh-and-blood women behind Europe’s national myths – warning against turning figures like Joan of Arc and Lady Godiva into ‘poster girls and propaganda tools’ for crafting national identities. Join Ramirez as she uncovers the true stories behind the tall tales. Chaired by Jean Menzies.

events.title: Simon Armitage, Hanan Issa & Peter Mackay: Poetry of the People
events.blurb: ‘Poetry is not only dream and vision,’ Audre Lorde wrote, ‘it’s the skeleton architecture of our lives.’ Join three brilliant national poets – Simon Armitage (UK Poet Laureate), Hanan Issa (Poet Laureate for Wales), and Peter Mackay (Makar of Scotland) – as they reflect on the idea of a national poetic identity, art’s place in responding to the world, and the power of poetry for its own sake (expect a few poems from each of them too!). Chaired by Hannah Lavery.

events.title: Tari Lang: My Neighbour, The Dictator
events.blurb: At the age of 14, Tari Lang’s life took a turbulent turn when both of her parents were imprisoned without trial during Indonesia’s 1965 coup. In My Neighbour, The Dictator, Lang provides a touching portrait of navigating crushes and curfews as a teenager, against the backdrop of dictatorship and tyranny. She joins us to discuss coming of age in the midst of a volatile environment, and how she found herself caught between wide-eyed adolescence and revolution. Chaired by Zinnie Harris.

events.title: Pop in and Play
events.blurb: Come and play with us! Everyone is welcome for our 30-minute guided sessions of fun and games, ideal to keep your wee ones busy. We know that great stories can come from great playtimes (no matter your age) so on your marks… get set… imagine!

events.title: Colin Grant: What We Leave We Carry
events.blurb: Colin Grant is renowned for his compelling work documenting the experiences of migrant communities, from the Windrush generation to his own Caribbean family. What We Leave We Carry: Voices of Migration to Britain saw him travelling the UK, taking in profound stories of love, loss, and arrival. Join Grant alongside contributors, including Chief Executive of Scottish Refugee Council, Sabir Zazai, and poet Clementine E Burnley, as they unpack the complexities of belonging and the emotional weight of what’s left behind. Chaired by Esa Aldegheri.

events.title: Simukai Chigudu, Gabriel Gatehouse & Sarah Wynn-Williams: Are You Sure?
events.blurb: In the era of strong men and keyboard warriors, changing your mind can seem like the ultimate weakness. But how does that leave room for uncertainty or change? Couldn’t we all stand to be a bit more flexible in our thinking? Join political scientist Simukai Chigudu who challenges the stories we inherit and journalist Gabriel Gatehouse, fresh from the frontlines of conspiracy culture. Also featuring Sarah Wynn-Williams. Check back soon for more details.

events.title: Alex Kadis: Big Nobody
events.blurb: Described by Pandora Sykes as ‘riotously funny and immensely touching’, Alex Kadis’ novel, Big Nobody, spins us into 70s East London, where Connie dreams of stardom... even if she has to kill her own father to get it. Drawing from her previous life as a music journalist (including a stint as features editor at Smash Hits in its legendary heyday), join Kadis to celebrate the strength of teenage dreams, the madness of first love, and what it takes to be somebody. Chaired by Nicole Abadee.

events.title: George E Osborn: Video Games, Politics, and the Battle for Global Influence
events.blurb: Video games are played by – and connect – billions of people worldwide, meaning that, beyond entertainment value, they hold incredible potential for influence. In Power Play, leading game industry expert George E Osborn reveals how authoritarians, extremists, and populists have taken full advantage of this, co-opting the industry to develop games that promote their worldviews. Today, he delves into gaming and geopolitics, toxic communities, and how one of our favourite hobbies is being weaponised for political purposes. Chaired by Caro Clarke.

events.title: A Verse of Poets
events.blurb: Join your host, Beth Cochrane, for a glittering line-up of poets from across Scotland. From Scots Scrievers to Gaelic singers, Edinburgh Makars to Edwin Morgan Poetry Award-winners, tonight’s roster use their poetry – sometimes tender, sometimes uplifting, sometimes downright raucous – to explore everything from the journey of diaspora to the naming of unspeakable desires. Featuring: Clementine E Burnley, Ceitidh Chaimbeul, Taylor Dyson, Hannah Lavery, Michael Mullen, and Andrés N Ordorica. You won’t want to miss this.

events.title: Saara el-Arifi & Nikita Gill: Of Queens and Goddesses
events.blurb: We’re thrilled to welcome back two outstanding talents this year, who’ve both chosen powerful, complex women to inspire their latest works. Poet Nikita Gill, whose novel Hekate breathes new life into the Greek goddess of witchcraft through heart-thudding verse, joins Saara el-Arifi, the Faebound author turning her hand to historical fiction with Cleopatra – a re-imagining of the iconic queen’s life through a Black woman’s lens. Strap in for an unapologetically feminist meeting of minds. Chaired by Jean Menzies.

events.title: Rosa Beltrán: Free Radicals
events.blurb: Rosa Beltrán’s electric novel, Free Radicals, has had to be reprinted three times in her native Mexico since it was published in 2021; now this ‘best-kept secret’ of global literature joins us to celebrate its English edition. A visionary yet intimate epic spanning three generations of women and six decades of seismic events in the history of Mexico, and the world, Beltrán today explores how the changes which happen within us are intertwined with those in the society surrounding us. Chaired by Ali Millar.

events.title: Who Runs the News?
events.blurb: In our fast-shifting media landscape, the rise of independent news organisations comes at the same time as long-reigning  face claims of bias and dwindling public support. What are these institutions doing to mediate the risk of reputational damage, and what tensions has this shift created among readers, audiences and journalists, alike? Join journalists including Ash Sarkar (Contributing Editor at Novara Media, author of Minority Rule) and Douglas Fraser( outgoing Business and Economy Editor at BBC Scotland) to discuss to the changing face of mainstream news and the role audiences play in holding these organisations — both new and established — to account. Chaired by Sarah Manavis.

events.title: Sara & Cariad's Weirdos Book Club — Live
events.blurb: Calling all weirdos and book-loving pals! Comedians, authors, and friends, Sara Pascoe and Cariad Lloyd, invite you to their Weirdos Book Club, lovingly described as ‘a space for the lonely outsider to feel accepted and appreciated’. Join them in the Spiegeltent tonight as they present a very special live edition of the podcast, which has previously included guests like Naomi Klein, Graham Norton, and Nish Kumar. Chatting to Amy Annette, amongst other guests to be announced.

events.title: Susan Orlean: Joyride
events.blurb: For four decades, legendary New Yorker journalist Susan Orlean has illuminated other people’s lives with wit and forensic curiosity. In Joyride, she revisits a career that reshaped narrative nonfiction – from cults and cab drivers to orchids and origami – while revealing the private heartbreaks and leaps of faith behind the bylines. Today Orlean, also the author of The Orchid Thief (adapted by Charlie Kaufman to become the 2002 film Adaptation) reflects with Hannah McGill on turning her virtuoso reporter’s gaze inward.

events.title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
events.blurb: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers with Ailie Finlay.

events.title: Marc Mierowsky: A Spy Amongst Us
events.blurb: It’s 1706, and Edinburgh's streets are a powder keg as the Scots protest the planned union with England. But as Marc Mierowsky’s A Spy Amongst Us thrillingly recounts, the English government had a very unorthodox secret service working to sabotage Scotland’s independence. It was led by a bankrupt and thrice-pilloried author – none other than Daniel Defoe. Join Mierowsky today to uncover espionage and propaganda from London to the Highlands, and the unknown story of a distinctly modern political campaign. Chaired by Brian Taylor.

events.title: Writing Things: A Poetry Workshop with Vona Groarke
events.blurb: What do the things we keep with us, show off, and carry from place to place, say about us? And how can that be harnessed as a shortcut, a signpost, a start? Join Ireland Professor of Poetry Vona Groarke (Infinity Pool) for a two-hour poetry writing workshop – an exploration and probing of objects for a possible haul of meaning, stories, or significance. There will be writing, plus thinking and talking about writing. And, of course, there’ll be poems too.

events.title: Sara Sheridan: The Jewel Keepers
events.blurb: A dangerous, long-guarded secret, a high-stakes treasure hunt through history, and a puzzle that stretches back generations – Sara Sheridan returns to the Festival with her immersive, Edinburgh-set novel, The Jewel Keepers. Join Sheridan, author of The Fair Botanists (Waterstones Scottish Book of the Year 2022), as she chats about the real historical events amid the dramatic fiction, plus what she discovered during her exclusive behind-the-scenes access to Edinburgh Castle while researching the novel. Chaired by Ashley Douglas.

events.title: Sensory Stories with Ailie Finlay
events.blurb: Join storyteller Ailie Finlay from My Kind of Book for 20 minutes of inclusive sensory storytelling fun! This is an exciting and engaging session for everyone but particularly suitable for children with additional needs and their families and friends.

events.title: Bring Back the Smile with Dean Atta
events.blurb: When you love someone, it feels wonderful. When they’re not around any more, it can be hard to know what to feel. Come and hear the uplifting story of Auntie’s Bangles, about two little cousins learning to celebrate the joy their auntie leaves behind by remembering the jingle-jangle of her bracelets. Poet (and recent BAFTA winner!) Dean Atta will help little ones find their own way to celebrate someone they’ve lost in a get-together full of hope.

events.title: Tiffany Jenkins: Strangers and Intimates
events.blurb: Perceptions of privacy and our right to it have changed across centuries and cultures, but in the age of surveillance and social media, populations are giving it away at an unprecedented rate. Discussing Strangers and Intimates, which the New Scientist called ‘the sort of history book which makes you look at all history anew’, cultural historian Tiffany Jenkins celebrates the past, present, and politics of the idea of private life, and examines what we may be losing.

events.title: Jan Carson: Few and Far Between
events.blurb: Surreal times call for surreal stories. Jan Carson’s Few and Far Between imagines an alternative history in which a community marooned on a haunted archipelago – a supposed utopia built to escape the Troubles – is now sinking under its own secrets. One of Northern Ireland's most imaginative writers and author of The Fire Starters and The Raptures, Carson joins us to unpack identity, community, redemption, and telling stories in order to survive history. Chaired by Niamh Ní Mhaoileoin.

events.title: Steve Crossan & Alan Finkel: Inside the Machine
events.blurb: An unmissable conversation with two fascinating figures at the forefront of global scientific innovation: Alan Finkel, former Chief Scientist of Australia and founder of the global certification organisation Proudly Human, and Steve Crossan, founding member of the pioneering DeepMind project. From seemingly impossible breakthroughs to the real-world impacts of rapid change, hear their views on the next stages of AI development, and what it means for big tech, governments, and ordinary citizens alike. Chaired by Dr Shannon Vallor.

events.title: Jimmy Wales: The Seven Rules of Trust
events.blurb: As trust in billionaire-owned social media platforms continues to plummet, it’s astonishing to see how crowd-sourced knowledge bank, Wikipedia – once a byword for dubious accuracy – has built up its readers’ faith to become one of the internet’s most clear-sighted information sources. Maintaining confidence in a landscape of untruths is important to Wikipedia’s legendary founder Jimmy Wales. We’re thrilled to welcome this key figure of the online age to discuss his book The Seven Rules of Trust. Chaired by Heather Parry.

events.title: The Front List: Kae Tempest
events.blurb: Kae Tempest is a phenomenon of words as a multi-award-winning poet, playwright, songwriter – and novelist. Renowned for his electric live performances, Tempest joins Michael Pedersen to celebrate his new heart-breaking, soul-building, decade-in-the-making novel, Having Spent Lift Seeking. Expect powerful reflections on family and forgiveness, redemption and atonement, the courage it takes to be seen, and the transformative power of love. Mixing performance and conversation, this is bound to be spellbinding and unique event from a generational talent.

events.title: Sensory Stories with Ailie Finlay
events.blurb: Join storyteller Ailie Finlay from My Kind of Book for 20 minutes of inclusive sensory storytelling fun! This is an exciting and engaging session for everyone but particularly suitable for children with additional needs and their families and friends.

events.title: What If...? with Tom Schamp
events.blurb: What if your bed was a sandcastle? What would bunny toast look like? What IS the most awesome thing on wheels? Well, best-selling author-illustrator Tom Schamp has explored all these brilliant things and more in his amazing books What If? and Wheels. Come along and meet him in a fun-filled story-building event to wake up your imagination.

events.title: Olga Wojtas: Miss Blaine's Prefect and the Parcel of Rogues
events.blurb: It’s 1788, Burns-mania is sweeping Edinburgh, and a time-travelling librarian has enlisted the teenage Walter Scott to help solve a mysterious murder – it could only be an Olga Wojtas novel. The maven of cosy crime is back with Miss Blaine’s Prefect and the Parcel of Rogues, the sixth in her series about unlikely sleuth, Shona McMonagle. Join for an hour of escapism as Wojtas takes us on a magical mystery tour of the Scottish Enlightenment. Chaired by Alice Tarbuck.

events.title: Sophie Pinkham: The Oak and the Larch
events.blurb: From the Mongol invasion to the days of the Tsars, the Soviet Union to Putin’s war in Ukraine, Russia is a nation with a difficult and bloody history. It’s also a country containing nearly a fifth of the world’s forested land. Today historian and Comparative Literature professor Sophie Pinkham discusses The Oak and the Larch, telling the story of the centuries-long entanglement between Russian history, identity, and landscape – and what this means for all of us. Chaired by Caroline Eden.

events.title: Simukai Chigudu: Chasing Freedom
events.blurb: Oxford University’s associate professor of African politics, Simukai Chigudu is part of the ‘Born Free’ generation, raised as colonial rule ended in Zimbabwe. In Chasing Freedom, he details a childhood steeped in Britishness – from Shakespeare to cricket – before being forced to leave the country as it descended into political violence and economic collapse. Join Chigudu discussing his remarkable story: that of a boy shaped through his parents’ stories and by the great currents of late 20th century history. Chaired by Dina Nayeri.

events.title: Sanna Marin & Nicola Sturgeon: How to Lead a Country
events.blurb: What does it take to lead a country with both courage and compassion? How do you balance hope with pragmatism; a personal life with a public one? In their memoirs Frankly and Hope in Action, former Scottish First Minister Nicola Sturgeon and former Prime Minister of Finland Sanna Marin reflect on political careers with refreshing honesty. Don’t miss their extraordinary conversation with Talat Yaqoob about the challenges, rewards, and history-making decisions that defined their leadership.

events.title: Sensory Stories with Ailie Finlay
events.blurb: Join storyteller Ailie Finlay from My Kind of Book for 20 minutes of inclusive sensory storytelling fun! This is an exciting and engaging session for everyone but particularly suitable for children with additional needs and their families and friends.

events.title: Bella Mackie: Claws Out
events.blurb: How to Kill Your Family author Bella Mackie is renowned for crime romps that skewer exactly the kind of people you (secretly) love to see skewered. Today she launches Claws Out! - her hotly anticipated new novel. When Diana Leyland sets her sights on a new romantic target, she doesn’t bet on his entitled daughter being determined to drag Diana’s murky past into the light. Because three dead husbands isn’t just unlucky – surely, it must be murder?

events.title: Vona Groarke & Tom Pow: The Poet’s Attention
events.blurb: Scotland and Ireland have always punched above their weight in the world of poetry. Today we welcome two of their most beloved poets: Vona Groarke and Tom Pow. Slippages and transformations abound in Infinity Pool, Ireland Professor of Poetry Groarke’s exhilarating new collection. In The Vulnerability of Precious Things, Pow examines the life and philosophies of Simone Weil, crafting a work of imaginative empathy. Don’t miss the pair discussing and reading from their new work today. Chaired by Marjorie Lotfi.

events.title: Elizabeth Finkel & Caitjan Gainty: Beyond Reasonable Doubt
events.blurb: Journalism to the law, academia to government – the institutions that underpin society rely on an evidence-based, expert-informed approach. Yet in this post-truth age, uninformed opinion can carry the same weight as rigorous research. Today, Devi Sridhar chairs a robust discussion on doubt and certainty with award-winning science journalist Elizabeth Finkel – who, in Prove It, unpacks the key elements of, and necessity for, scientific thinking – and medicine historian Caitjan Gainty – whose Healthy Scepticism illustrates where legitimate doubt has helped healthcare advance.

events.title: Underwater Escapades with Chris Riddell
events.blurb: Splish splash – dive into a world of mermaids and mayhem! You’re going to be swept away by the latest storybook from much-loved author-illustrator Chris Riddell. In A Mermaid’s Rescue, shy Atalanta chases through Mer City to rescue her vanished best buddy. But will time run out? Chris tells you how he gets stunning stories and pictures to pour from his pen, and how you can too. An event for budding artists, storytellers, and mermaid fans alike.

events.title: Writing Magical Realism: A Workshop with Jan Carson
events.blurb: Jan Carson ‘captures the absurdity and beauty of life’ like no other according to Sara Baume – so, who better to lead this masterclass on magical realism, where the fantastical meets the mundane, than the luminous author of Few and Far Between. Join Carson to dive into the tradition of magical realism, then play with exercises that’ll get you thinking about how you can weave the surreal into your own stories of the everyday. Suitable for all – just bring your notebook, pen, and imagination.

events.title: Louise Welsh: The Cut Up
events.blurb: We’ve waited patiently for four years and the time’s finally come – but can our favourite queer auctioneer-turned-accidental-detective stay out of trouble? In The Cut Up, Louise Welsh – Scottish literary legend and author of cult classic The Cutting Room – takes us back into the shady world of Rilke’s Glasgow. Always fabulously entertaining, with a razor-sharp wit, Welsh chats with us today about her third foray into this gritty series. Chaired by Kirsty Logan.

events.title: M John Harrison: The End of Everything
events.blurb: Master of science fiction M John Harrison returns with his first novel since 2020's Goldsmiths Prize-winner, The Sunken Land Begins to Rise Again. In The End of Everything, Phillip Tennent, who collects washed up artefacts from the Channel, comes across a mysterious shapeshifting object that threatens to destabilise everything he thinks he knows. Today, Harrison joins us to discuss the post-apocalyptic, satirical adventure and how it chronicles the limits of human understanding. Chaired by Ann Landmann.

events.title: Donal Ryan: Where are the Kings
events.blurb: Donal Ryan is fast becoming an Irish national treasure. Full of heart, his writing tackles the moments that make up a life with compassion and humour. In Where are the Kings, a young man navigates family secrets, loss, and the changes that growing up brings. Hear the prize-winning author of works including Heart, Be at Peace, and From a Low and Quiet Sea chat about coming of age, living with grief, and big messy families. Chaired by Sasha de Buyl.

events.title: Dean Atta: Big Man
events.blurb: Is there anything Dean Atta can’t do? As well as being a beloved YA and children’s author, ‘one of poetry’s greatest modern voices’ according to Gay Times, and a recent BAFTA winner for his short animation Two Black Boys in Paradise, the Festival favourite now presents his highly anticipated adult literary debut, Big Man. Join Atta today as he discusses his tender yet playful story and its themes of queer aging, race, and living authentically. Chaired by Colin Grant.

events.title: Rock the Boat: Poetry Open Mic
events.blurb: Whether you’re ready to hit the mic or just keen to soak up the vibes, this event has you covered. Our friends at Push the Boat Out – Edinburgh’s genre-bending international poetry festival – host a special edition of their vibrant monthly open mic to celebrate dynamic contemporary poetry and performance. So, sit back and enjoy, or take to the stage and showcase your own work. Check back soon to find out how to get involved.

events.title: Edwin Morgan Trust: Poetry, Performance, and Prizes
events.blurb: This lively showcase, hosted by Ryan Van Winkle, features some of the best of Scotland’s contemporary poetry scene. Discover the talented young poets shortlisted for 2026’s Edwin Morgan Poetry Award as they perform their work right before the big reveal of this year’s prize-winner. Plus – celebrate the launch of the new, edited collection of Edwin Morgan’s groundbreaking multimedia poetry, A Home in Space, with editors Greg Thomas and Julie Johnstone. Joined by Tom Bailey, Emmett Coleman, Zainab Imran, Flora Leask Arizpe, Kate Millar and Caitlin Palmer.

events.title: Alistair Moffat: The North Sea
events.blurb: Alistair Moffat has always combined lyrical prose with fascinating storytelling, leading to over 30 acclaimed books delving into the wonders of Scottish history and beyond. The North Sea: Along the Edge of Britain sees the renowned historian travelling from Kent to Fair Isle to better understand our relationship with the sea. In this captivating event, Moffat shares tales of his seaside pilgrimage: from well-worn seaside towns to windswept island monasteries, and above the waves to below.

events.title: Ashley Hickson-Lovence & Matthew Rice: Art/Work
events.blurb: Ashley Hickson-Lovence and Matthew Rice push the limits of form to explore the tension between work and ‘the work’ of a writing life. Set during a single 12-hour nightshift, Rice’s Plastic mixes poetics, memoir, and ekphrasis to illuminate the world of factory labour. Hickson-Lovence’s About to Fall Apart, written as a single paragraph that unfolds across one frantic weekend, is a masterclass in voice. Come along for an engrossing discussion on practice, labour, and where creativity resides. Chaired by Colin Grant.

events.title: Graeme Macrae Burnet: Benbecula
events.blurb: Graeme Macrae Burnet’s Benbecula, part of Polygon’s acclaimed Darkland Tales series, explores a forgotten, real-life triple murder in the remote Hebrides, in characteristicly immersive, unsettling prose. As his narrator’s mind slowly fractures, Burnet asks: how do tragedy and isolation distort memory and selfhood? The Booker-shortlisted author of His Bloody Project chats crime and punishment, unreliable minds, and his pull to the territory where history, fiction, and psychological darkness collide. Chaired by James Crawford.

events.title: Edward Fishman & Carl Benedikt Frey: You Can’t Fight Progress
events.blurb: Former US State Department official Edward Fishman and Oxford academic Carl Benedikt Frey take us right into the real-life thriller that is the global struggle for power and progress. Fishman’s Chokepoints lays bare the economic battlegrounds that define modern-day war, while Frey’s How Progress Ends warns that even rapid progress stagnates if innovation falters. Join them to discover these intersecting arenas, where 21st century geopolitics really plays out. Chaired by Richard Brass.

events.title: Simon Armitage: New Cemetery
events.blurb: A local beauty spot becomes a graveyard; a poet walks its boundary. Today, UK Poet Laureate Simon Armitage discusses and performs from his latest collection, New Cemetery, in which the new graveyard near his West Yorkshire home inspires a radiant, wry meditation on grief, nature, and time. Hear one of our finest poets of landscape, loss, and the strange comedy of being alive, reflect on changing landscapes, personal loss, and the life-enhancing power of poetry. Chaired by Peggy Hughes.

events.title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
events.blurb: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers with Tracey Corderoy.

events.title: Pop in and Play with Dads Rock
events.blurb: Are you ready to rock? Dads Rock are here and they want to make some noise with you! Join the friendliest dads in town for a fun-filled session of stories and play.

events.title: Alan Davies: White Male Stand-Up
events.blurb: After the events of Just Ignore Him, Alan Davies’ hugely moving and best-selling memoir, there was still a lot of life to come for the comic, actor, and QI staple. Today Davies discusses the next chapter of his life, White Male Stand-Up, recounting his awkward journey from the comedy circuit (alongside some other well-known names) to life-changing fame as Jonathan Creek – and his reluctant acceptance that he’s maybe best known for a bank advert… Expect honesty, laughter, and achingly personal tales of success and excess (and their dangers) with one of UK comedy’s best loved figures. Chaired by Zara Janjua.

events.title: Train Tales
events.blurb: Let's take a train to Imagination Land! Join our pals from LNER for Train Tales, a chance to hop aboard for stories and brilliant activities to help little ones get ready for future journeys. There might even be a very special guest...

events.title: Shared Reading with Open Book
events.blurb: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session. Each session will explore a chapter from a debut book from this year’s Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading materials will be provided on the day.

events.title: Kate Foster: The Repentants
events.blurb: Betrayal flows through Kate Foster’s chilling new novel: the story of two women, bonded forever in their exile to the world’s most desolate prison. Based on the real-life attempt by Scottish landowners to annex Iceland, The Repentants tackles shame, sin, and survival while transporting us to a harsh 18th-century landscape. Join Foster, the Women’s Prize-longlisted author of The Maiden, as she shares the thrill of reimagining the lives of women of the past. Chaired by Natalie Jayne Clark.

events.title: Stories in Space with Ross MacKay
events.blurb: When a determined tractor swaps farm life for an out-of-this-world adventure, silliness ensues. Join author Ross MacKay for a delightful event all about his awesome new book, Tractors in Space: a Saturn-surfing, moon-bouncing, galaxy-hopping good time exploring the wonders of the universe with heaps of heart and new friends aplenty. You’ll have an absolute blast.

events.title: Fresh Words: Northern Writers’ Awards
events.blurb: It’s lunchtime, but there’s no need to doomscroll over your meal deal. Be the first to discover the literary stars of the future instead. In partnership with Scottish Book Trust and other leading UK talent spotters, this lively event showcases electrifying new voices, so grab your seat before everyone else does. Today, we partner with New Writing North’s Northern Writers’ Awards, hearing readings from an amazing line up of writers, featuring Letty Sharpe, Beth Thompson, Cindy Withjack, Ross Crawford and Andy Grace Edwards.

events.title: Steve Brusatte & Jackie Morris: Birds – Evolution and Extinction
events.blurb: Every Jurassic Park fan knows dinosaurs eventually evolved into birds, and in The Story of Birds, leading palaeontologist and film adviser Steve Brusatte recounts that thrilling, 150-million-year journey towards the creatures we know today. In The Book of Birds, meanwhile, artist Jackie Morris (with writer Robert Macfarlane) celebrates avian species at risk of extinction with soulful paintings and words. From prehistoric beginnings to modern vulnerability, Brusatte and Morris discuss the joys and mysteries of our feathered friends. Chaired by Hannah Rudman.

events.title: Doggy Treats with Tracey Corderoy (Steven Lenton has cancelled)
events.blurb: Shifty McGifty and Slippery Sam are back with more mischief in their new book The Robber Ghost. The former thieves-turned-baker-dogs will be finding out if their doggy detective skills can save the day! Join author Tracey Corderoy for some spook-tacular storytelling, drawing and heaps of audience participation.

events.title: Polly Barton, Daniel Hahn & Anton Hur: In Other Words
events.blurb: How does a book survive a journey between languages? Three exciting literary translators and writers join forces for a lively chat about their craft. Polly Barton (Butter, Hunchback), Daniel Hahn (A General Theory of Oblivion, Pelé: The Autobiography), and Anton Hur (Cursed Bunny, Love in the Big City) unpack why human translation still matters in an age of AI and how translation is more than a bridge between cultures: it’s a creative act in its own right. Chaired by Adam Biles.

events.title: Gwen Adshead: Unspeakable
events.blurb: Silence can be as powerful as what is said aloud, as pioneering psychiatrist and psychotherapist Dr Gwen Adshead very well knows. For decades, she’s helped patients navigate painful and distressing life events, witnessing their courageous journeys to be free of fear and shame.
