She joins us with Unspeakable, for a conversation less about trauma, and more survival – the ‘what comes next’. Discover the language that allows us to move forward, to transform, and to hope. Chaired by Ali Millar.

events.title: The Front List: Diana Gabaldon
events.blurb: It's been 35 years since Claire Randall first slipped through time, landing in the arms of Jamie Fraser and at the heart of a love story spanning centuries. Diana Gabaldon’s Outlander novels have since become a bona fide sensation as a smash-hit TV series, with the ‘Outlander effect’ credited with revolutionising Scottish film, TV production, and tourism alike. Join Gabaldon for this special anniversary event to reflect on the inspirations behind the adventures of the Fraser clan and how creating the ‘Sassenach’ changed her life forever.

events.title: Dinner: A Table Talk with Meera Sodha
events.blurb: Every week, thousands turn to Meera Sodha’s Guardian columns and cookbooks for vibrant veggie inspiration, be it her Sichuan-style aubergines or unbelievably creamy vegan mac and cheese. Watch a master at work as she prepares a favourite dish from the smash hit Dinner, and shares how cooking healed her after ‘a baby and a breakdown’ threatened to snuff out her spark. Ticket includes: a welcome drink and a delicious food taster.

events.title: Music Day!
events.blurb: What have music and books got in common? Find out with the Book Festival team, and help us use rhythm and simple instruments to make brilliant new poems. Everyone is welcome, and no experience is needed so come for the drop-in session, stay for the inspiration!

events.title: Baby and Toddler Rhymetime with Craigmillar Books for Babies
events.blurb: Let your little stars twinkle with Craigmillar Books for Babies in this special Baby and Toddler Rhymetime. Enjoy bouncy songs, tickly rhymes, and lots of cuddles, while building attachment and bonding with your little ones.

events.title: Callum McSorley: Rat Race
events.blurb: DCI Alison McCoist is Glasgow’s most unpopular detective, and the thrillers starring her are the filthiest, funniest crime novels in Scotland. Callum McSorley's latest novel Rat Race closes the MacIlvanney Prize-winning trilogy as McCoist chases a drug-dealer-turned-marathon-runner through a tangle of gangsters and bent cops. A new star of crime discusses violence and humour, urban Scotland, and ending the series with an absolute belter. Chaired by Kim Sherwood.

events.title: Garth Cartwright & Madeline Potter: The Travelling Life
events.blurb: Caroline Eden talks to two writers shedding light on the experiences and vibrant traditions of Romani communities in Europe. Madeline Potter discusses her personal and revealing The Roma: A Travelling History, while Garth Cartwright, author of Princes Amongst Men: Journeys with Romani-Gypsy Musicians, charts a journey through what –  in 2005 – were thought to be the ‘badlands’ of Romania, Bulgaria, and the former Yugoslavia.

events.title: Jane Harper: Last One Out
events.blurb: Australia’s Crime Queen, Jane Harper, is internationally renowned for her atmospheric thrillers. In fact, her 2016 smash hit, The Dry, sparked a whole wave in Aussie publishing of small-town crime fiction, a phenomenon that’s come to be known as ‘Outback Noir’. We’re so excited to welcome Harper to Edinburgh today – hear her chatting about her new novel, Last One Out, a claustrophobic and engrossing study of fractured families and communities. Chaired by Lee Randall.

events.title: Scots Rhymetime with Craigmillar Books for Babies
events.blurb: Dinnae fash yersel like a craw on a waw, come doon and join Craigmillar Books for Babies with a special Scots Rhymetime! Enjoy Scots rhymes, songs, lots of cuddles, and fun to support attachment and bonding with your wee ones.

events.title: Jeremy Hunt: Can We Be Great Again?
events.blurb: A major figure in the previous Conservative UK Government, Jeremy Hunt has served as Chancellor and Foreign Secretary, and led the Culture and (controversial) Health briefs. His Can We Be Great Again? is a timely read in a world of shifting geopolitical faultlines. Rebutting the idea that the UK is in inevitable decline on the international stage, join Hunt as he sets out a new take on how our influence can be used to positively affect global democracy, migration, trade, and climate. Chaired by Peter MacMahon.

events.title: Music Day!
events.blurb: What have music and books got in common? Find out with the Book Festival team, and help us use rhythm and simple instruments to make brilliant new poems. Everyone is welcome, and no experience is needed so come for the drop-in session, stay for the inspiration!

events.title: Mohammed Hanif: Rebel English Academy
events.blurb: Mohammed Hanif – the Booker-longlisted author of A Case of Exploding Mangoes – brings his fierce combination of incendiary wit and political nerve to his thrilling new novel, Rebel English Academy. Fusing slapstick with state-of-the-nation reckoning to hilarious, harrowing effect, Hanif sets love, protest, and state violence on a collision course in late-70s Pakistan. Join him today as he discusses authoritarianism, dissent, and why satire is one of the sharpest tools for telling the truth. Chaired by Daniel Hahn.

events.title: Colin Bramwell & Ryan Van Winkle: Poetry in Practice
events.blurb: Two singular voices in Scottish poetry, Colin Bramwell and Ryan Van Winkle, join the Festival to share new work and discuss their practice of bringing poetry to wider audiences, both on and off the page. Both poets play with questions of communication and connection: Bramwell’s Fetch explores the boundaries of Scots and English to question a host of binaries, while Van Winkle’s intimate Get Closer considers how we remember and misremember, shaping memory through experience. Chaired by Ellen Renton.

events.title: Turi King: The Secrets of Our DNA
events.blurb: Renowned genealogist Professor Turi King uses her renowned skills to reshape our understanding of our ancestors, from unearthing their previously known medical conditions to their surprising international connections. In 2012, King led the identification of King Richard III’s body; in 2025, she co-presented Channel 4's documentary, Hitler’s DNA; today, she unpacks The Secrets of Our DNA, exploring how DNA shapes our world, from trial outcomes to species survival. Chaired by Jo Sharp.

events.title: Translating Shakespeare: A Workshop with Daniel Hahn
events.blurb: Three of Daniel Hahn’s literary translations have been longlisted for the International Booker Prize, and today he turns his attention to translating the work of William Shakespeare. This workshop, drawing from Hahn’s If This Be Magic, explores what reading the Bard’s work in a host of other languages (like Hungarian, Japanese, and Swahili) can tell us about translation, the author, and language itself. Participants don’t need familiarity with any languages besides English. No knowledge of Shakespeare needed.

events.title: Meera Sodha: A Life Well Fed
events.blurb: When craving comfort and nourishment, Meera Sodha is a name we all trust. As a food columnist for the Guardian and author of bestselling cookbooks like Fresh India and Dinner, Sodha spreads her skill for flavourful recipes as generously as the icing on her cardamom dream cakes. Today she shares how cooking has truly fed her, from the kitchen smells of her Ugandan-Indian childhood home, to the dishes that brought her back from the brink of burnout. Chaired by Stuart Cosgrove. Chaired by Julie Lin.

events.title: Chris Brookmyre: Quite Ugly One Evening
events.blurb: Chris Brookmyre is an icon of Scottish crime fiction and a regular Festival favourite. This year, he returns with Quite Ugly One Evening: a zeitgeisty locked-cabin mystery set on a cruise celebrating an extremely questionable 1960s TV series... Who better to investigate than legendary journalist Jack Parlabane, 30 years since his first appearance in Quite Ugly One Morning? Natalie Jayne Clark chairs a conversation as energising, satirical, and irreverent as the author himself.

events.title: Tice Cin & Jacqueline Crooks: City Soundscapes
events.blurb: Big city life is equal parts exhilarating and gruelling in these lyrical, inventive novels from Tice Cin and Jacqueline Crooks. In Safe Spaces and Sky City, young women navigate the ups and downs of London living. Throughout, music is the beat that sustains them, a connective thread that sparks friendships, provides belonging, and offers a way through, or a way out. Today the authors come together to discuss navigating grief, fostering community, and finding home. Chaired by Anahit Behrooz.

events.title: Graeme Armstrong: Raveheart
events.blurb: Named one of Granta’s Best of Young British Novelists in 2023, Graeme Armstrong is back with his hotly anticipated second book Raveheart. Set in the heart of Scotland’s rave subculture, this pacy new novel follows a band of rebels and misfits as they try to resurrect illegal warehouse parties in the face of a dystopian right-wing regime. Join Armstrong as he discusses this ‘hilarious, tragic, and incredibly clever’ look at modern Scotland. Chaired by Ali Millar.

events.title: Imani Thompson: Honey
events.blurb: It’s not every day that a debut novel sparks a ferocious 10-way bidding war, but Imani Thompson’s Honey is that dazzling. In a conversation that promises to be as darkly entertaining as the book itself, comedian Sophie Duker joins Thompson to delve into the mind of Honey’s murderous protagonist, Yrsa: the perfect vehicle for a razor-sharp exploration of race, desire, and female rage. Don’t skip this chance to see a bona fide star on the rise.

events.title: Simon Kuper: World Cup Fever
events.blurb: This August, doubtless hot on the heels of Scotland’s victorious 2026 campaign (!), sports journalist Simon Kuper joins us with World Cup Fever. An attendee of every World Cup since 1990, Kuper chronicles the fervour of this global sporting fiesta, one which brings nations to a standstill and sends fans on incredible journeys just to be there. Tears, joy, controversy, inspiration, politics – this is the story of football, its magic and tumultuous history combined. Chaired by Stuart Cosgrove.

events.title: Citizen Collective: 26 Collective Street
events.blurb: It’s New Year’s Eve on 26 Collective Street, a century-old building filled with stories and poems – open a door and dip into a life. Join us as families party, dogs cower from fireworks, and friends (and strangers) bring in the bells. But something has happened that risks ruining the night… This event has been co-created by young people from the Citizen Collective (our online creative writing group for young adults) and professional poet, Ryan Van Winkle.

events.title: Margaret Busby: Part of the Story
events.blurb: The UK’s first Black female publisher and editor of groundbreaking anthologies Daughters of Africa and New Daughters of Africa – it’s hard to overstate Margaret Busby’s impact on literary culture these last 50 years. It is an honour to welcome her to the Festival. Busby joins us to discuss her life’s work as a champion of Black voices and Part of the Story, which charts her journey from precocious girl in Ghana to publishing pioneer. Chaired by Hannah Chukwu.

events.title: Sama Sama: A Table Talk with Julie Lin
events.blurb: In her debut cookbook, Sama Sama, Malaysian-Scottish chef Julie Lin explores how food can nourish our very souls, acting as a bridge that connects us to our roots. Following a sold-out event with us last summer, Lin – who's a favourite on BBC One’s Saturday Kitchen and founder of Edinburgh's hippest new eatery, Tacos Lah kitchen in Bonnie & Wild food hall – joins us again in Elliott’s Studio for this immersive Table Talk event. Bring your curiosity and your appetite as Lin teases out the vibrant ingredients that define her as she shares stories from the heart and whips up something delicious for you to try. Chaired by Ailidh Forlan.

events.title: Ann Pettifor: The Global Casino
events.blurb: Political economist and director for PRIME, Ann Pettifor is famous for predicting the 2008 global financial crash. In this conversation she unpicks how the cost of your weekly shop, monthly bills, car, house, and holiday aren't just linked, they're fixed by faceless firms and funds operating in the shadows. Today, she discusses her new book The Global Casino: How Wall Street Gambles with People and the Planet, exposing a corrupt system while offering a truly sustainable alternative. Chaired by Mure Dickie.

events.title: The Book Festival Ceilidh
events.blurb: Nothing brings people together like a good birl! Join us tonight for a barnstorming dance, complete with one of Scotland’s favourite ceilidh bands, The Occasionals. Never ceilidh-ed before? Have no fear, Strip the Willow newbies and Dashing White Sergeant experts are all welcome as a live caller takes us through the steps of traditional Scottish dances. Maybe you’ll even do-si-do with your favourite author.

events.title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
events.blurb: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Check website for today's author.

events.title: Benny Higgins: A Life in Reading
events.blurb: At fifteen, growing up football-mad on a Glasgow housing scheme, Benny Higgins received a letter from his grandfather — a Clydeside docker — with a list of books he wanted Higgins to read. It changed everything. The former chair of the National Galleries of Scotland, whose remarkable career has spanned finance, culture, and public life, reflects on how reading and the arts shaped his path, and why culture remains essential to who we are. Chaired by Amina Shah.

events.title: James Macintyre: Power with Purpose
events.blurb: His time in Number 10 may have been short, but more than 15 years since leaving Downing Street, Gordon Brown continues to wield significant influence. In Power with Purpose, former BBC1 Question Time producer and political correspondent James Macintyre provides an intriguing and definitive portrait of Brown, from his political birth to election defeat and life beyond. Today, Macintyre joins us to discuss his latest biography about a true political powerhouse, with a formidable legacy. Chaired by Ruth Wishart.

events.title: Pop in and Play with Cròileagan Dhùn Èideann
events.blurb: Would you like to introduce your wee one to Gaelic? Join the playleaders from Cròileagan Dhùn Èideann, Edinburgh’s Gaelic playgroup for 0-5s, to learn some simple Gaelic words and phrases together with your child, through songs, stories, and play. A relaxed and fun-filled session; no prior knowledge of Gaelic required.

events.title: Polish Bookbug
events.blurb: Witamy Wszystkich! Czas na polską sesję ‘BookBug’! Join us for this special Polish Bookbug Session – enjoy songs, stories, and rhymes in this fun, interactive event. All welcome, no prior knowledge of the Polish language necessary.

events.title: Margaret Drabble: The Great Good Places
events.blurb: Childhood homes, cherished libraries, coastal sanctuaries – how do the places we remember shape who we are? Drawing on decades of writing and observation, literary legend Margaret Drabble blends memoir, essay, and short fiction in The Great Good Places, a profoundly moving meditation on time, memory, and the process of ageing. Today, she brings her astonishing wit and intelligence to discuss the pleasures and complexities of looking back on a life deeply lived. Chaired by Lennie Goodings.

events.title: Peggy Brunache & Carrie Gibson: The Fight to be Free
events.blurb: Historian Carrie Gibson’s The Great Resistance chronicles thousands of acts of defiance in the fight to end slavery across the Americas and the Caribbean. She appears alongside Dr Peggy Brunache, University of Glasgow lecturer in the history of Atlantic slavery and director of the Beniba Centre for Slavery Studies, which works to amplify the voices of history. Join us for this insightful conversation about insurrections, revolutions, and modern questions about social and racial inequality. Chaired by Alex Renton.

events.title: Translation Surgery: A Workshop with Polly Barton (120 mins)
events.blurb: Polly Barton is the acclaimed translator of books including Asako Yuzuki’s publishing sensation, Butter, Mieko Kanai’s Mild Vertigo, and Saou Ichikawa’s Hunchback. In this fun problem-solving session for practising translators, Barton invites you to bring along the translation issue that’s been irking you. From the granular to the abstract, witness the extraordinary creative forces unleashed when translators put their minds together! All languages and experience levels are welcome.

events.title: Dan Jones: The Green Man
events.blurb: A learned monk. A town in turmoil. A mystery that may destroy faith itself. Dan Jones' The Green Man is a gripping medieval mystery set in 1367 Berwick, where children are disappearing, Scottish raiders menace the borders, and the old pagan ways are creeping back. The spec-fiction writer and author of Man O'War discusses reason and belief, religious panic, and why a novel set seven centuries ago feels disturbingly like our own times. Chaired by Calum Barnes.

events.title: Make Friends with a Panda with Maisie Chan
events.blurb: Can you imagine a panda so gorgeous, she became world famous? It actually happened! And you can hear her incredible story when you join author Maisie Chan for a cosy chat about her new picture book, Chi Chi the Panda. From Chi Chi’s birth in China, to living in zoos all around the world, to becoming the best-known animal in England… it’s a BAMBOO-zling journey. The perfect event to show young animal lovers what made this panda so special.

events.title: Francis Spufford: Nonesuch
events.blurb: To read Francis Spufford’s literary fantasy Nonesuch is to be grabbed by the hand and pulled, screaming with delight, through a version of wartime London where statues talk, timelines bend, and fascism entangles with dark magic. From Booker-longlisted Light Perpetual to his last novel Cahokia Jazz, Spufford is always deft at drawing timely truths out of alternate realities. If you need a fresh perspective on how to keep fighting the good fight, don’t miss him. Chaired by Chitra Ramaswamy.

events.title: Marion Gibson, Mairi Kidd & Steven Veerapen: The Witching Hour
events.blurb: At a time when women’s rights are once again at threat across the world, it’s perhaps no wonder that our fascination with the witch-hunts of the 1600s still burns bright. Today, we’re joined by Mairi Kidd (Newes of Witches), Marion Gibson (Witchland), and Steven Veerapen (Witches: A King’s Obsession) – the authors of brilliant new books that touch on themes of paranoia, moral panic, and obsession. What can our witch-hunting past warn us about the world of today? Chaired by David Greig.

events.title: The Front List: Tom Holland
events.blurb: Historian and The Rest is History podcast co-host Tom Holland describes The Lives of the Caesars, written by Seutonius 2,000 years ago, as having ‘the quality of a very highbrow gossip column’. His new translation of this influential work illuminates the lives of the first 12 Roman emperors, exploring their leadership strategies, policy crises, eccentricities, even their sex scandals. Join Jenny Niven chatting with a writer who’s revolutionised popular history – not to be missed by anyone who thinks about the Roman Empire even infrequently.

events.title: Baking and the Meaning of Life: A Table Talk with Helen Goh
events.blurb: After a decade developing recipes (including that chocolate tahini cake) as Ottolenghi’s pastry chef, Helen Goh brings her brilliance into the spotlight with her own book, Baking and the Meaning of Life. If you’ve got a sweet tooth, you can’t miss the chance to taste a Goh-made treat straight from the oven, as she shares the personal histories behind her delectable creations. Ticket includes: a welcome drink and a delicious food taster. Chaired by Simon Preston.

events.title: Teach Us Your Language
events.blurb: We love that the Book Festival brings together people from all over the world, and that includes you. Whether you're a grown-up or very new to talking, if you can speak (even a wee bit) of a different language then come along to our drop-in session and teach us. We speak baby, and even our littlest visitors will be very welcome to contribute!

events.title: Anton Hur & Lee Seong-bok: That Summer’s End
events.blurb: Regarded as one of South Korea’s most influential poets, Lee Seong-bok is the author of eight extraordinary poetry collections and numerous other works, including Indeterminate Inflorescence, his acclaimed book of aphorisms which boasts fans including the members of K-Pop megahit band, BTS. It’s a real honour to welcome Seong-bok to the Festival, talking about his intoxicatingly beautiful new work, That Summer's End, alongside Anton Hur, the International Booker Prize-shortlisted translator of the collection. Chaired by Andrew McMillan.

events.title: Sara Baume: Opening Night
events.blurb: What can friendship teach us about art – and art about friendship? In Opening Night, Sara Baume traces her growing bond with exiled American painter Mollie Douthit, from soup and punishing Atlantic swims in West Cork to grappling with complex questions about community and nationality, neurosis, mysticism, love, and pain. Hear the much-admired author of Spill Simmer Falter Wither open up about companionship, creativity, and the soul-stirring spell art can cast over a life. Chaired by Peggy Hughes.

events.title: Frances Crawford & Jennie Godfrey: Community Secrets
events.blurb: We all love a good secret, especially when they’re as gripping as they are wildly entertaining. In Frances Crawford’s A Bad, Bad Place, a 12-year-old girl and her nan are dragged into the hunt for a murderer, while Jennie Godfrey’s The Barbecue at No.9 follows a Live Aid watch party as it turns sinister. In this lively event, Crawford and Godfrey talk writing mystery and plotting the perfect thriller with splashes of humour. Chaired by Mary Paulson-Ellis.

events.title: Alexander McCall Smith: Perfectly Prolific
events.blurb: From the Georgian splendour of Edinburgh's New Town to the sunlit plains of Botswana, Alexander McCall Smith conjures incomparable worlds of warmth, humour, and humanity. This year, The Prime of Bertie Pollock brings fresh adventures to 44 Scotland Street, while The Big Cats Dance Party reunites us with the incomparable Mma Ramotswe. Join the knight of Scottish letters for a conversation full of generous-spirited storytelling. Chaired by Zinnie Harris.

events.title: Polly Atkin & Gillian Best: Pain, Presence, Possibility
events.blurb: How do we live well in bodies that don’t make life easy? In Swimming the Seasons, Polly Atkin finds relief, freedom, and joy in year-round immersion in wild water. In Chronic, Gillian Best combines cutting-edge pain research with her own search for understanding. Together, they explore pain and disability, swimming and self-knowledge, and the possibilities of paying closer attention to body, mind, and the natural world. Chaired by Roxani Krystalli.

events.title: Polly Barton & Aea Varfis-van Warmelo: Lies, Crushes, and Karaoke
events.blurb: Obsession and karaoke. Lies and self-sabotage. In What Am I, A Deer? and Attention-Seeking Behaviour, Polly Barton and Aea Varfis-van Warmelo bring fierce formal invention to two bitingly funny, mercilessly perceptive novels about trying to translate yourself into someone more palatable. Barton, the fearlessly original essayist and translator of Asako Yuzuki's bestselling Butter, joins Varfis-van Warmelo - a sharp, edgy new voice in fiction - to unpick confession, compulsion, authenticity, and whether we can ever truly escape ourselves. Chaired by Irenosen Okojie.

events.title: Daniel Hahn: If This Be Magic
events.blurb: Why is Hamlet longer in Italian? How do you land a Shakespearean joke in German? And why are Lady Macbeth’s pronouns such a headache? In If This Be Magic, seasoned translator Daniel Hahn dives gleefully into the seemingly impossible task of translating Shakespeare, revealing how English words stretch, fracture, and misbehave across languages. Today Hahn celebrates close reading and linguistic absurdity to show how changing every word can bring Shakespeare thrillingly back to life. Chaired by Adam Biles.

events.title: Soph’s 30 in 30: A Table Talk with Sophie Macfie
events.blurb: As the culinary force behind social media sensation ‘Soph’s Plant Kitchen’, Sophie Macfie has led the charge for a better understanding of the protein and fibre potential of plant-based cooking – deliciously delivered through mouthwatering dishes to her almost 2 million followers. Join Macfie (and her trusty blender) as she whips up fresh, quick, nutrition-packed recipes from Soph’s 30 in 30. Ticket includes: a welcome drink and a delicious food taster. Chaired by Ailidh Forlan.

events.title: Close Read: Intro to Gaelic Literature
events.blurb: In our popular Close Read series, a brilliant author guides you through a deep-diving discussion of a classic text or genre that’s inspired them. Think of it as an event blending friendly book club vibes with insightful study notes. Today, novelist Mairi Kidd (The Specimens) provides an introduction to Gaelic literature, using her expert knowledge to share some gems. Expect a fun, enthusiastic workshop to please the eye – and ear. No prior experience of Gaelic needed.

events.title: See Yourself in Writing with Maisie Chan
events.blurb: If you want to be a writer, it’s time to get started! Lucky for you, Maisie Chan, the brilliant author of Danny Chung Does Not Do Maths, is here to get you inspired. Ask all the questions you've always wanted to put to a published author (How do I write memorable characters?, Where do I even begin?) and start developing your own ideas. Everyone’s welcome, whether you’re totally new to writing or sitting on jotters full of plots.

events.title: Caroline Elton: Looking After
events.blurb: Born in the 1940s, when autism was barely understood, Lionel was treated as ‘a peculiarity’. Looking After: Autism, Family and End of Life Care is his life story told by psychologist and academic Caroline Elton – his little sister. From their formidable mother refusing advice to institutionalise her young son, to his musical passions, and their shifting familial bonds, Elton shares Lionel’s complex portrait, talking today about carving space for the legacies we leave behind, and finding the life-affirming, tender moments, and love within. Chaired by Caroline Elton.

events.title: Jeremy Hunt & John Kampfner: Great vs Better
events.blurb: What does Britain have to offer on the world stage in the 21st century? Are we leaders, or is there much to learn? And in seeking to fix Britain’s challenges, should we look close to home, or further afield? Join former Chancellor and Foreign Secretary Jeremy Hunt, author of Can We Be Great Again? Why a Dangerous World Needs Britain and journalist John Kampfner, author of Braver New World: The Countries Daring to Do Things Others Won’t for a thought-provoking discussion, chaired by Liz Lloyd, on the state of our nation, and others who do things differently.

events.title: Myths and Magic with Carlos Sánchez
events.blurb: When dark magic and druids meet dragons and delicious desserts, you know it’s Rune time! Get sucked into Carlos Sánchez’s latest mind-warping graphic novel, Rune: The Tale of the Winged Sorceress. Discover what it takes to plan a comic, learn how Carlos got the idea to use sign language as a superpower for his deaf heroine Chiri, and throw yourself into some fantastical drawing challenges in a creative session that’ll leave you spellbound.

events.title: Mona Chalabi: Psychedelics, Shifty Exes, and Objectivity in Journalism
events.blurb: Mona Chalabi is a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist who converts complex data into arresting illustrations, often using text and sound to make people stop and rethink. She was named a Royal Designer for Industry – the highest accolade that a UK designer can receive – in recognition of her talent for making the intangible tangible. From capturing the enormity of wars in Palestine, Congo, and Sudan, to how hijabis are depicted on screen, Chalabi talks to Heather Parry about how 'design helps to structure our moral universe.'

events.title: Luke Wright: Later Life Letter
events.blurb: In Later Life Letter, his fiercely moving memoir-in-poetry, Luke Wright explores the effect of his own ‘later life letter’ – the document written by a social worker to an adopted child, detailing their journey from birth to adoption. Wright chats today about this tender, beautiful collection – full of wit and warmth and championed by the likes of John Cooper Clarke, Hollie McNish, and Lemn Sissay – then brings the story off the page with a dazzling performance. Chaired by Emma Collins.

events.title: Beyond the Margins: Poetry in Motion
events.blurb: We believe that everyone has a story to tell and that stories help us make sense of our world. Over the spring, community members from the Streetreads Library joined forces with poet Hannah Lavery and illustrator Katie Quinn to create poetry and imagery exploring Edinburgh through their eyes, as people who have experienced homelessness in the city. Join them as they share their bold, unfiltered take on the Edinburgh the tourists don’t see.

events.title: Kenneth R Rosen & Odd Arne Westad: Polar Power
events.blurb: Greenland was thrust into the global spotlight by President Donald Trump announcing his intent to acquire the Arctic territory, by hook or by crook. But what sits under the ice that’s so vital to geopolitics? Who better to unravel the puzzle than Cold War historian Odd Arne Westad (The Coming Storm) and American journalist and war correspondent Kenneth R Rosen (Polar War) who join us today to dissect this literal coldest of wars, and explore why the region is so vital to our futures. Chaired by Edward Wong.

events.title: So Mayer: Bad Language
events.blurb: Language shapes the structures of our world: Who gets to speak? Who is silenced? Who is harmed in this imbalance? In their stunning blend of memoir and manifesto, Bad Language, So Mayer draws on their multi-lingual childhood and cultural texts (from the Torah to the Brothers Grimm) to interrogate how language has been used – and abused – across their own life. Join us for a rousing conversation about taking back language for protest and pleasure. Chaired by Sasha de Buyl.

events.title: Meet the Winners: International Booker Prize 2026
events.blurb: The International Booker Prize, the world’s most influential award for translated fiction, champions literature from around the world, fostering an engaged global community of writers and readers whose experiences transcend national borders. The award brings international attention to both the author and translator with the prize divided equally between them. Join us as Emeritus Director Fiammetta Rocco speaks to the winners of 2026’s International Booker Prize (supported by Bukhman Philanthropies) about their work and the art of translation.

events.title: Darren McGarvey: Trauma Industrial Complex
events.blurb: What makes us share our inner world with strangers? Darren McGarvey is a broadcaster, hip-hop artist, and campaigner, and his newest book, Trauma Industrial Complex: How Oversharing Became a Product in a Digital World, reflects on the commodification of trauma. The Orwell Prize-winning author of Poverty Safari shares his experience building a career through rapping and campaigning, and examines how personal narratives have been repackaged into digestible confessionals for public consumption. Chaired by Ali Millar.

events.title: Jem Calder & Jack Edwards: Inklings Book Club — Live
events.blurb: Jack Edwards has a knack for knowing exactly which novels will set our hearts alight, and today ‘the internet’s resident librarian’ sits down with Jem Calder for a special live recording of the Inklings Book Club podcast. Discovered by Sally Rooney, who first published his writing in The Stinging Fly, Calder’s spot-on debut, I Want You to Be Happy, explores the listlessness, precarity, and wild joy of being in your 20s and 30s will make for an unmissable chat.

events.title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
events.blurb: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers with Morag Hood.

events.title: Masud Husain: Our Brains, Our Selves
events.blurb: The brain’s workings are essential to our identity, says Oxford neurology professor Masud Husain, winner of 2025’s Royal Society Science Book Prize. Our Brains, Our Selves unveils case studies of seven patients, including a man who ran out of words and a woman whose memory loss made her believe she was having an affair with her own husband. Join Husain to explore our most complex organ. Chaired by Devi Sridhar.

events.title: Move It Day
events.blurb: It’s Friday and we need to streeeeetch! We’ll be using inspiration from some of our favourite stories to move, dance, and have lots of fun. These sessions will be a perfect opportunity to get those end of the week wriggles out, while answering the very important question: what would the Gruffalo’s favourite yoga pose be? Everyone is welcome to join in however they’d like to.

events.title: Shared Reading with Open Book
events.blurb: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session. Each session will explore a chapter from a debut book from this year’s Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading materials will be provided on the day.

events.title: Bookbug with Edinburgh Libraries
events.blurb: Hello everyone! It's time for Bookbug. Join Edinburgh Libraries for songs, stories, and rhymes in this much-loved, fun, interactive event. We heard that we might get a visit from the one and only Bookbug, so you can even get a photo, a hug, and a cheeky high-five! Part of the Scottish Book Trust's Early Years programme.

events.title: Fresh Words: Gutter Magazine
events.blurb: It’s lunchtime, but there’s no need to doomscroll over your meal deal. Be the first to discover the literary stars of the future, instead. In partnership with Scottish Book Trust and other leading UK talent spotters, this lively event showcases electrifying new voices, so grab your seat before everyone else does. Today, we partner with Gutter Magazine’s Finishing Your First Book programme, hearing readings from an amazing line-up of writers including CL Glanzing, Adam Gordon, Helen Lewis-McPhee, Amy Macrae, Sukhada Tatke and Eris Young

events.title: Andrew Lownie: The Rise and Fall of the House of York
events.blurb: Royal biographies are commonly drama-filled but in Andrew Lownie’s Entitled, scandal, corruption, and cover-ups take centre stage. The historian’s dual biography of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and Sarah Ferguson draws on four years of research, FOI requests, and hundreds of interviews, tracing the reputational collapse of the pair, from their links with Epstein to misconduct in office. Lownie joins us in conversation, offering an insight into his research and the grift and corruptions of ‘high society’. Chaired by Lucia Osborne-Crowley.

events.title: Nao-Cola Yamazaki, Polly Barton & Charlotte Goff: Writing the Interior
events.blurb: Nao-Cola Yamazaki is a name you’re about to hear everywhere. Their intimate novellas, Beautiful Distance and Don’t Laugh at Other People’s Sex Lives, were smash hits in Japan, now published in English with stunning translations by Charlotte Goff and Polly Barton. Both stories deal with devotion: the deference employees are expected to show corporations in Japanese ‘salaryman’ culture, and the yearning that mounts between an art student and his much older tutor. Don’t miss this sparkling conversation with three rare talents. Chaired by Sash de Buyl.

events.title: Nick Barber & Helen Pilcher: The Mind-Body Connection
events.blurb: An eye-opening conversation on the psychology of medicine. Pharmaceutical expert Nick Barber offers a guide for how to make the most of your medicines in How to Take Drugs, while This Book May Cause Side Effects sees neuroscientist Helen Pilcher explore the dreaded 'nocebo effect’. Gavin Francis chats to them both, tackling topics ranging from better health and advocating for yourself, to understanding how medicines work on the brain, and even rethinking the mind-body connection.

events.blurb: Hello everyone! It's time for Bookbug. Join Edinburgh Libraries for songs, stories, and rhymes in this much-loved, fun, interactive event. We heard that we might get a visit from the one and only Bookbug, so you can even get a photo, a hug, and a cheeky high-five! Part of the Scottish Book Trust's Early Years programme.

These sessions will be a perfect opportunity to get those end of the week wriggles out, while answering the very important question: what would the Gruffalo’s favourite yoga pose be? Everyone is welcome to join in however they’d like to.

events.title: The Front List: Colson Whitehead
events.blurb: Colson Whitehead is one of America’s most skilled and essential storytellers, holding the horrors of history in one hand and big-hearted humanity in the other. After consecutive Pulitzer Prize-winners, The Underground Railroad and The Nickel Boys, he concludes his acclaimed Harlem trilogy with Cool Machine: a portrait of hustle in 1980s New York. Join Whitehead, who is uniquely qualified to parse America’s past and present, for an energising conversation on why we can’t move forward without looking back.

events.title: Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi: The Ghost of the Mountains
events.blurb: There’s only a handful of people who have been anywhere near the vicinity of a snow leopard, and this event will probably be the closest most of us will ever get: a wonder-filled conversation with biologist Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi, who’s spent decades studying these elusive creatures. Hear about The Ghost of the Mountains, his thrilling account of intrepid exploration, dedicated conservation work, and the transcendent experience of encountering a snow leopard in the wild. Chaired by Caroline Eden.

events.title: Simon Sebag Montefiore: The Cauldron
events.blurb: In this timely, thought-provoking event, bestselling author and historian Simon Sebag Montefiore discusses The Cauldron: The Making of the Modern Middle East, his compelling history on the intricacies and complexities of this tumultuous yet magnetic region. Talking with us today, Sebag Montefiore considers how modern states are made, the power of personality leadership, and the latest violent chapter of a rapidly evolving region. Chaired by Nida Alahmad.

events.title: Come On, Smile! with Morag Hood
events.blurb: Seahorse is grumpy and he needs cheering up... or does he? Come along to this funny, gentle event with Morag Hood, creator of wonderful stories like I am Bat, Colin and Lee, Carrot and Pea, and now the brand new book: Seahorse is Furious. Find out all the ways Seahorse’s friends try to make him smile and get some nifty ideas about how to deal with your own feelings. See you there!

events.title: Yuliana Ortiz Ruano: Carnaval Fever
events.blurb: In Yuliana Ortiz Ruano’s Carnaval Fever, a girl’s coming of age in the Afro-Ecuadorian community of Esmeraldas pulses with music, dance, and the fierce love of the women who raise her. But beneath the celebration, shadows press in: poverty, migration, and the threat of male violence. Daniel Hahn joins one of Latin America’s most exciting voices, an English PEN Translates Award-winner, to discuss identity, resilience, and writing that you feel in your body.

events.title: Move It: Build Cars, Trucks, and Anything That Goes!
events.blurb: Vroom vroom, it’s Friday, and we’re getting this show on the road! Want to build your very own moving vehicle from cardboard and other recycled stuff? You’ve parked in the right place. Inspired by Richard Scarry’s classic book, Cars and Trucks and Things That Go, join the Festival’s Communities Team to hear the story and enjoy an afternoon filled with crafting fun. We’ll bring the materials, you bring your creative ideas.

events.title: Catherine Cho & Saima Mir: Destiny and Dynasty
events.blurb: As the old saying goes, the family that slays together, stays together – and it’s even messier in the criminal underworld. Saima Mir's Deliverance (the final part in her compelling Jia Khan trilogy) and Catherine Cho’s thrilling debut, The Devoted, both tackle the complexities of life within criminal dynasties. Today, two terrific voices in fiction join Sam Baker to delve into the perilous world of organised crime.

events.title: Nandini Das: This Little World
events.blurb: British Academy Book Prize-winner, Nandini Das, is Professor of Early Modern Literature and Culture at Oxford University. Her newest work, the captivating This Little World: A New History of Tudor and Stuart England, bursts the idea of England existing in isolation in the 16th and 17th centuries, uncovering its critical international connections through tales of merchants, migrants, sailors, travellers, and spies. Join Das to discuss nationhood and her resonant new view of England’s global past. Chaired by Samira Ahmed.

events.title: Hilary Cottam & Sarah O’Connor: New Ways of Working
events.blurb: We’re continually told that the AI revolution will forever alter our relationship with work, yet need that change be for the worse? Enjoy an invigorating discussion with two authors offering upbeat proposals for the future of work: Orwell Prize-winning Financial Times journalist Sarah O’Connor, whose We Are Not Machines explores humans learning to master destabilising new technology, and innovator and change-maker Hilary Cottam, whose The Work We Need reimagines labour as a force for collective good. Chaired by Jarred McGinnis.

events.title: Perfectly Dystopian with K L Kettle
events.blurb: A new world has dawned and it’s perfect. But… it’s not real. In Control Alter Delete – K L Kettle’s speculative thriller – gamer Hal could win everything she ever wanted, or her entire reality could come crashing down. How will she choose what she really wants? Join K L as she chats about writing, finding hope in dystopia, and how she created the incredible world of the book.

events.title: Sophie Mackintosh & Stephanie Sy-Quia: Loves, Lies, and Longing
events.blurb: What’s better than reading a book that pulses with emotional electricity and the thrill of forbidden love? Reading two! In Permanence, Sophie Mackintosh (Booker-longlisted author of The Water Cure) imagines a world where adulterers can test their love without fear of consequence, while Stephanie Sy-Quia's A Private Man fictionalises the crackling connection between her Catholic priest grandfather and a theology teacher. They compare notes on passion as a constructive and destructive force with Sasha de Buyl.

events.title: Jem Calder & Derek Owusu: New Masculinities
events.blurb: When a debut author 'discovered' by Sally Rooney meets one of Granta’s Best Young Novelists, you can count on a fresh, fiercely intelligent exchange of ideas. Be in the room today with Jem Calder and Derek Owusu as they discuss their novels of modern masculinity and authenticity in the digital age, then run (don’t walk) to put I Want You to Be Happy and Borderline Fiction right at the top of your TBR pile. Chaired by Andrés N. Ordorica.

events.title: Scottish Parliament Elections: Where to From Here?
events.blurb: The votes are counted, and 2026’s Scottish Parliament election has delivered a winner – but has it delivered a workable government? Will Scotland see stable leadership, or a parliament shaped by deals, compromises, and constant risk of fracture – and what questions does the result pose for Westminster too? Today's panel of experts – including polling specialist Sir John Curtice, journalist David Torrance, and political advisor Liz Lloyd – go beyond the headlines to unpack the result, map the new balance of power, and reflect on this next chapter of Scottish politics. Chaired by Nicola McEwan.

events.title: The Good Immigrant: 10 Years On
events.blurb: Featuring powerful and impassioned writing by 21 writers of colour, The Good Immigrant unflinchingly interrogates what it really means to be Black, Asian, and Minority Ethnic in Britain today. On the 10th anniversary of this generation-defining collection, editor Nikesh Shukla joins some of the book’s award-winning contributors – including comedian and commentator Nish Kumar – to reflect on themes of otherness, belonging, and what, if anything, has really changed over the past decade. Himesh Patel and Chimene Suleyman will also be participating in this event.

events.title: Memory and Story: A Workshop with Jarred McGinnis
events.blurb:
Memories are mercurial things and can be recounted differently even by those who shared an experience. Join Jarred McGinnis, author of There is No Meant to Be, for an all-senses-engaged interactive workshop which transforms your funny, profound, and most chaotic memories into works of creative writing. Bring along a family member, friend, or other individual with whom you share recollections and explore just how different our stories can be, even when their starting point is the same. No writing experience needed. 
Individual writers can sign up, however many of the exercises will be carried out in pairs, drawing on shared experiences.

events.title: Winners, Liars… and Crafts with Aleema Omotoni
events.blurb: Stately homes, rich-kid rivals, a high stakes competition to win a multi-million-pound fortune – Aleema Omotoni’s twisty new YA thriller, Winners and Liars, serves up dark academia with a side of Knives Out. In other words: unmissable. Hear Aleema talk about the book’s themes of wealth, loss, history, and black girlhood, then get your craft on and make something together with other readers.

events.title: Patrick Freyne & Séamas O'Reilly: Deadly Serious
events.blurb: Two of Ireland’s sharpest wits come together for a conversation about finding the funny in the darkest of places. Patrick Freyne – novelist, journalist, and a viral sensation for his Irish Times piece about Ireland and the Royal family – gets a band back together in Experts in a Dying Field, with unexpected consequences. Seasoned Observer journalist Séamas O’Reilly’s Prestige Drama follows the cast of an in-production drama in Derry as they solve the mystery of their missing leading lady. Chaired by Peggy Hughes.

events.title: Natalie Jayne Clark: The Malt Whisky Murders
events.blurb: Sit back, take a tipple, and delight in the darkly comic world of Tartan Noir novel, The Malt Whisky Murders. When Eilidh and her wife Morag open the first women-owned distillery in Scotland, they find themselves up against protest, scandal, nosy neighbours, intrusive TV crews… and two perfectly preserved bodies hidden in a pair of whisky barrels. Join this uniquely immersive talk and whisky tasting with poet, writer, and whisky ambassador, Natalie Jayne Clark. Chaired by Simon Preston.

events.title: David Keenan: Boyhood
events.blurb: It starts in 1979 with the abduction of a young boy outside a Glasgow football ground. But David Keenan’s Boyhood soon swells into a journey of grief and recovery, past and present, imagined and real. The author of cult classic This Is Memorial Device returns with his love letter to Glasgow, a novel Irvine Welsh is calling ‘a complete triumph’. Today, Keenan introduces this extraordinary and multilayered story about youth, dreams, and magic. Chaired by Ali Millar.

events.title: Jenni Fagan: The Delusions
events.blurb: What happens when love collides with the laws of eternity? In The Delusions, Festival favourite Jenni Fagan (author of Luckenbooth and The Panopticon) imagines an afterlife run by cosmic bureaucracy: newly dead souls are processed, delusions extracted, and humans may soon become a banned race. Today, Fagan chats about love and defiance, satire as survival, and enlisting her incomparable imagination to try and capture the terrible fragility of life on earth. Chaired by Zoe Venditozzi.

events.title: Édouard Louis: The Weight of Where We Come From
events.blurb: Few writers expose the intimate violence of class and family with the force of international sensation Édouard Louis. In Monique Escapes and Collapse, two searing novels about lives shaped by poverty and abuse, the author of The End of Eddy trains his fearless gaze on his mother and brother. Hear his extraordinary blend of emotional intensity and sociological sharpness as he talks shame, escape, reinvention, and what it takes to break the cycles we inherit. Chaired by Adam Biles.

events.title: Alison Irvine & Imogen Willetts: Burn Bright All Night (Jack Parlett has cancelled)
events.blurb: Flamboyance shines throughout culture in art, entertainment, protest, and fashion. It’s at its shiniest when darkness descends and bars and clubs thrust their doors open. Join Alison Irvine – author of Barrowland – and historian Imogen Willetts – whose intoxicating Up All Night is a tour through history’s wildest parties – as they chat about the power of collective hedonism and the unique power of bodies in a room. Chaired by Rachel Ashenden.

events.title: Samantha Shannon: Among the Burning Flowers
events.blurb: Samantha Shannon is an expert worldbuilder. With her million-copy bestseller The Priory of the Orange Tree (a feminist reimagining of Saint George and the Dragon) she gave us a portal into a magical universe of fire-breathing creatures so real you almost felt the heat. We’re delighted to have her brilliant mind back at the Festival to unpack Among the Burning Flowers, a prequel that imbues this well-loved world with a darker backstory of heartbreak and human resilience. Chaired by Irenosen Okojie.

events.title: Mischief and Mayhem with Mark Watson and Pals
events.blurb: Fringe legend and unforgettable Taskmaster contestant Mark Watson is also the author of almost a dozen books, including his latest, deliciously entertaining novel, One Minute Away. Today, Watson becomes our inaugural ‘Bookmaster’ and is joined by a cast of fellow funny and bookish folks – including Zara Janjua, Sanjeev Kohli, and Marjolein Robertson – for a gab about books, writing, and comedy, as well as some hilarious, playfully competitive surprises.

events.title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
events.blurb: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Check website for today's author.

events.title: Jarred McGinnis: There Is No Meant to Be
events.blurb: Outlaw ancestors, family ghosts, a near-fatal accident, and a refusal to behave like a proper memoir: Jarred McGinnis’ There Is No Meant to Be unearths the legends, violence, tenderness, and absurdity that run through his family line, dismantling rules and literary boundaries to ask what truly makes a life. Hear the author of The Coward on care, fatherhood, disability, and why even the hardest lives can still contain laughter. Chaired by Dan Richards.

events.title: Supertato Silliness with Paul Linnet
events.blurb: Stories, songs, and silly times await in this event with the author of everybody’s favourite spud: Supertato! Join Paul Linnet to celebrate the release of the latest adventure, Supertato: Despicable Bean. The brand new book sees Supertato and squad go on a hilarious holiday where the heat is on. Find out if the gang make their getaway as a mean, green baddie returns to rile everyone up and cause some serious trouble.

events.title: A Birthday Party for… Isadora Moon
events.blurb: Mark your calendars, dust off your dancing shoes, and get ready to party! Loads of our favourite books have big anniversaries this year so we’re throwing some of them a special birthday bash. Come along today to celebrate 10 years since Harriet Muncaster published the first Isadora Moon book, Isadora Moon Has a Birthday. There’ll be storytime, party games, dancing, and singing as we wish our favourite half-fairy, half-vampire friend many happy returns.

events.title: Daisy Fancourt & Wayne McGregor: The Art of Health
events.blurb: What if you could dance yourself smarter? Or paint away pain? This fascinating discussion between world-leading scientist Daisy Fancourt (Art Cure: The Science of How the Arts Transform Our Health) and world-renowned choreographer Wayne McGregor (We Are Movement: Unlocking Your Physical Intelligence) draws on science, research, and lived experience to explore the power of art, and how engaging with music, movement, and creativity can improve your health and happiness in innumerable tangible ways. Chaired by Thangam Debbonaire.

events.title: Starting from the Truth: A Memoir Workshop with Catherine Cho
events.blurb: Above all else, memoir has to start from the truth. In this workshop led by Catherine Cho, Jhalak Prize-shortlisted author of Inferno: A Memoir of Motherhood and Madness, you’ll start thinking about where to begin when telling your own story. Together you'll unpack the structure and openings of published memoirs, using them as a springboard for your own writing, while exploring how memoirs can act as mirrors for the reader.

events.title: You are Ready! with Jodie Ounsley
events.blurb: There are loads of different ways to be strong, and who better to guide you through them than athlete and real-life Gladiator Jodie Ounsley (AKA Fury)? Off the back of new book Keep Smashing It, Jodie shares stories, advice, and tips which will give you the confidence to back yourself and smash barriers — something she’s done all her life, from playing professional rugby to becoming the first deaf Gladiator.

events.title: Meet the Star Kitties with Laura Ellen Anderson
events.blurb: If your idea of a PURR-fect day is one spent around some adorable kitty-cats, then you’ll want to meet Laura Ellen Anderson’s newest creations, the Star Kitties! And if you already know and love Amelia Fang and Rainbow Grey, then you’ll know that Laura’s artwork is pretty awesome. Get ready to see the world of her new story, Star Kitties: The Big Birthday Mystery, in glorious colour. It’s gonna be un-FUR-gettable!

events.title: Meet Supertato
events.blurb: Is it a bird, is it a plane? No! It’s a massive superhero potato, of course! Come along for a chance to meet Supertato and give everyone’s favourite vegetable a high-five and pose for a photo… just promise you’re not actually Evil Pea in disguise. Veggies unite!

events.title: Leap Into the World of Ballet with Steven McRae
events.blurb: Steven McRae is here to make your ballet dreams come true. Steven’s a principal dancer with The Royal Ballet and his brilliant new book, Anything Is Possible with Ballet, shows how dancing is for absolutely everyone. Come hear him chat about everything from jumps and positions, to taking care of yourself along the way. So, leap right in and celebrate self-belief. No ballet experience (or tutus) needed!

events.title: Lorraine Kelly: The Island Secret
events.blurb: A true Scottish national treasure, broadcaster, and bestselling author Lorraine Kelly needs little introduction. Hot on the heels of her debut novel, The Island Swimmer, she returns to Orkney with The Island Secret, which sees an unexpected visitor turn life upside down for Evie - who'd hoped to finally find some peace. As warm and engaging as her stories, Val McDermid chats to Kelly about drawing inspiration from the island she’s been visiting annually since 1985.

events.title: Rebecca Perry: May We Feed the King
events.blurb: A reclusive heritage curator, a long forgotten, reluctant king, and the uncanny merging of history and storytelling – T.S. Eliot Prize-shortlisted poet Rebecca Perry’s intricate debut May We Feed the King braids together two disparate lives, playfully floating between the present and an imagined past. Join Perry as she delves into this puzzle-box of a book which tackles history-as-narrative, the allure of power, and the magic of escapism. Chaired by Heather Parry.

events.title: Victor Mallet, Nikesh Shukla & Daniel Trilling: The Far-Right Has Risen
events.blurb: Across the world, the far-right is emboldened, on the rise, gathering support by demonising migrants, scapegoating minorities, and demanding the closure of borders. Join Financial Times senior world desk editor Victor Mallet (Far-Right France), author Nikesh Shukla (Hope Must Be Held In a Clenched Fist), and journalist Daniel Trilling (If We Tolerate This) for an urgent discussion about what’s causing this ongoing threat to global order, how it can be fought, and what it says about us. Chaired by Talat Yaqoob.

events.title: Donna Ashworth & Hannah Richell: Life Beyond Loss
events.blurb: Navigating loss is a path we will all have to tread. Donna Ashworth and Hannah Richell help us plot a course. An Ocean and a Day is Richell’s account of her journey through the first years following the death of her husband, Matt. Ashworth’s Loss is a specially selected collection of her poems for the bereaved. Join them for a moving conversation about grief, hope, and holding space for what comes next. Chaired by Sarah Gwonyoma.

events.title: Meet Supertato
events.blurb: Is it a bird, is it a plane? No! It’s a massive superhero potato, of course! Come along for a chance to meet Supertato and give everyone’s favourite vegetable a high-five and pose for a photo… just promise you’re not actually Evil Pea in disguise. Veggies unite!

events.title: The Front List: Lewis Goodall & Edward Wong
events.blurb: What’s the current state of the ‘special relationship’ between the USA and the UK? As America’s new approach to geopolitics redefines the global order, what engagement strategy is the UK taking, is it effective, and how on Earth do journalists keep up? In this 250th year since America separated from British rule, New York Times diplomatic correspondent Edward Wong and co-host of British podcast The News Agents Lewis Goodall take us behind the scenes of how to make sense of an unprecedented time in international relations, and what it means for the future of US-UK relations. Chaired by Liz Lloyd.

events.title: Have Lunch with Santiago Lastra
events.blurb: When a Michelin-starred chef invites you to lunch, you come hungry. Secure your front-row seat to Mexican Soul author Santiago Lastra’s masterclass in sour, smoky, and spicy flavours inspired by his Morelos upbringing. Usually behind the scenes at London restaurants KOL and Fonda, this is a rare chance to hear his tips firsthand and see (and sample) his artistry up close. Ticket includes: a welcome drink, a multi-course lunch, and specially paired wine on the table.

events.title: Relaxed Screening: You Donut Want to Miss This with Neill Cameron
events.blurb: Some of us thrive better in smaller, informal spaces. That’s why we’re putting on this relaxed screening for anyone with sensory sensitivities. You can watch the livestream of ‘You Donut Want to Miss This with Neill Cameron’ while being able to move around, come and go, and make noise in this friendly, chilled out space.

events.title: Lucy Caldwell & Nell Stevens: Short Story Magic
events.blurb: BBC National Short Story Award-winning Lucy Caldwell (author of Openings and These Days) and Nell Stevens (author of The Original and Somerset Maugham Award-winning Mrs Gaskell & Me) are both masters at catapulting you into characters’ lives, conjuring entirely new worlds in a matter of pages. In this conversation they discuss their new story collections, Devotions and The Good Time, talking stories of love, grief, haunted lives, emotional crossroads, and irresistible humour with Di Speirs.

events.title: You Donut Want to Miss This with Neill Cameron
events.blurb: Fresh from causing chaos on the pages of The Phoenix, Neill Cameron’s Donut Squad have taken the world by storm, one glazed, zany adventure at a time. Today, Neill presents another battle of the baked goods in Donut Squad: Make a Mess. Hear more about the antics of Jammyboi, Spronky, and salty seadog Caramel Jack (bagels strictly NOT invited).

events.title: Meet Supertato
events.blurb: Is it a bird, is it a plane? No! It’s a massive superhero potato, of course! Come along for a chance to meet Supertato and give everyone’s favourite vegetable a high-five and pose for a photo… just promise you’re not actually Evil Pea in disguise. Veggies unite!

events.title: Natasha Walter & Talat Yaqoob: A Feminist Response to Polycrises
events.blurb: Writers and activists Natasha Walter and Talat Yaqoob come together for a vital conversation on global feminism. In Feminism for a World on Fire, Walter calls for collective resistance beyond individualism, while Yaqoob’s edited collection, Building a Feminist Nation, explores practical feminist change in times of multiple crises. With women facing rights rollbacks across the world, and their safety and freedoms under attack, Walter and Yaqoob ask: how can feminism respond to a world on fire? Chaired by Roxani Krystalli.

events.title: Close Read: Mr Norris Changes Trains by Christopher Isherwood
events.blurb: In our Close Read series, a brilliant author guides you through a deep-diving discussion of a classic text or genre that’s inspired them. Think of it as an event blending friendly book club vibes with insightful study notes. Today, party historian Imogen Willetts (author of Up All Night: A History of Going Out) guides you through the simmering tensions and messy nights out of Christopher Isherwood's Mr Norris Changes Trains, an evocative novel of 1930s Berlin, and inspiration for the musical Cabaret.

events.title: Tara Menon & Cecile Pin: Lives in Aftermath
events.blurb: Tara Menon's stunning debut, Under Water, and Cecile Pin's exquisite Celestial Lights are two haunting novels of retrospection, in which private lives are altered by forces far larger than themselves: a lost friend on a post-tsunami Thai island; a husband and father hurtling towards a distant moon. From ecological catastrophe to the costs of ambition, they open up a poignant conversation about memory, love, sacrifice, and the ways we hold on to the people who define us. Chaired by Rachelle Atalla.

events.title: Get Bizzy with Benji Davies
events.blurb: Let’s dream up a new Bizzy Bear story! And let’s watch clever author-illustrator Benji Davies, creator of The Storm Whale, bring it to life with his amazing paints and pens! Roll up your sleeves and get arty as Benji takes you on his latest illustration adventure, Bizzy Bear Tractor Trouble, and tells you all about his brilliant Bizzy Bear world. A perfect event to develop early learning skills and spark imagination.

events.title: Friends vs Fiends with Rob Biddulph
events.blurb: Love stories with bite? Here’s a howling hit of an event with Rob Biddulph, of YouTube’s Draw with Rob fame. Prepare for your spine to be chilled as Rob reveals his new nailbiter, The Moonhaven Chronicles: The Last Wolf. Four friends sneak out after dark in a town where some people carry the werewolf gene. Watch out for the full moon… Explore fear, family, and friendships, with audience participation aplenty.

events.title: Sarah Perry: Death of an Ordinary Man
events.blurb: In Death of an Ordinary Man – an unflinching, tender work of non-fiction – Sarah Perry trains her gaze on the dying process itself, taking us to the bedside of her father-in-law as his life ends, just days after his cancer diagnosis. The author of The Essex Serpent and Booker-nominated Enlightenment reflects on why she chose to write about this intimate time of heightened experience and astonishment – a conversation as much about living as it is about dying. Chaired by Di Speirs.

events.title: Shida Bazyar: The Nights Are Quiet in Tehran
events.blurb: Laced with secrets, sorrow, and the longing of exile, The Nights Are Quiet in Tehran tells the human story of political upheaval. Shida Bazyar reveals the reality of leaving your homeland and living in hope, following one family from the Iranian Revolution to present-day Germany. Shortlisted for 2026’s International Booker Prize, it draws on Bazyar’s parents’ memories and the dissonance of witnessing Iran’s turmoil from afar. A rare chance to hear her reflections firsthand. Chaired by Marjorie Lotfi.

events.title: Derek Forbes: A Very Simple Mind
events.blurb: From their early days as late-70s Glasgow post-punks to the international success of ‘Don’t You (Forget About Me)’, bassist Derek Forbes was a key player in Simple Minds’ first decade. Having also recorded and performed with Iggy Pop, David Bowie, Big Country, Kirsty MacColl, and many others, the Scottish music icon arrives at the Festival brimming with anecdotes from his autobiography, A Very Simple Mind. He’ll even bring his guitar for a song or two. Chaired by Fiona Shepherd.

events.title: Leila Elder & Mahmud El Sayed: Future Histories
events.blurb: Where will the world be in 25 years? How about two centuries from now? Today, two writers with audacious imaginations are here to share their predictions. A pioneer of sci-fi genre Arabfuturism, Mahmud El Sayed foresees political unrest aboard a spaceship in The Republic of Memory. He joins Leila Elder, editor of the short story anthology, Iran +100, which imagines the country in the year 2053 - for a thought-provoking discussion about imagined futures. Chaired by Noor Hemani.

events.title: Mates, Magic, Mystery with Yassmin Abdel-Magied
events.blurb: Warm, funny, and a powerhouse of imagination, Yassmin Abdel-Magied chats about the first book in her new fantasy series featuring characters so relatable it feels like you’re reading about your own mates. Silverbrook: Yumna and the Golden Horse is about a quiet nothing-ever-happens town that suddenly comes alive with magic and secrets. When teens start developing powers and one of them disappears, it takes someone extraordinarily ordinary to get to the bottom of it all. Chaired by Alice Tarbuck.

events.title: Speak Up: A Spoken Word Poetry Workshop with Katie Ailes & Kevin Mclean
events.blurb: Join poets Katie Ailes and Kevin Mclean, directors of Scotland's award-winning Loud Poets, for this inspiring spoken word poetry workshop. Explore what makes dynamic, innovative spoken word poems, and then get stuck into exercises on writing for performance. Sharing work out loud can be scary, so the pair will share plenty of tips on how to kick nerves and build confidence performing onstage – and there’ll be an opportunity to practice at the mic. No experience needed.

events.title: Andrew Durbin: The Wonderful World That Almost Was
events.blurb: The Wonderful World That Almost Was  explores the lives of two key figures in New York’s art scene. Penned by Frieze Magazine editor, Andrew Durbin, it traces the relationship between Peter Hujar and Paul Thek: their first encounter in '50s Miami, their intense creative and sexual relationship in the '60s, their fall out in the '70s. Hear Durbin unpacking this love story of art, history, and the glamour and grit of mid-20th-century NYC. Chaired by Fiona Anderson.

events.title: Bias, Impartiality, and the Future of News
events.blurb: In an age of conflict, conspiracies, and unchecked AI generation, having news sources we can trust has never been more vital. But how does our media maintain balance on such rocky ground? Is complete impartiality the best way to tell a story? And how might emerging technologies bake bias into our journalistic landscape? Our panel tackling these pressing questions includes Lewis Goodall (The News Agents podcast), and Fergus McIntosh (The New Yorker). More exciting guests to be announced – check back soon for the full line-up.

events.title: Charlotte Higgins: Ukrainian Lessons
events.blurb: In 2022, Charlotte Higgins headed to Ukraine to cover a literary festival, an experience that transformed her life. Ukrainian Lessons: Art in a Time of War explores how culture is weaponised during times of war, the lasting impact on society, and how art so easily shifts from collateral damage to a central front. Hear the Guardian's chief culture writer delving into art as a form of resistance during devastating times. Chaired by Allan Little. Chaired by Fiona Bradley.

events.title: Brief Encounters with Buffy's Book Club
events.blurb:
Lizzy Hadfield has long been a tastemaker, but with Buffy’s Book Club she took London and New York’s literary scenes by storm. Join her at this special event to sip, socialise, and compare TBR lists with other discerning book lovers in celebration of Vintage Classic’s Brief Encounters collection. Enjoy a drink as ‘Bibliotherapists’ pair you with the perfect short novel for your taste – whether that’s an Edith Wharton ghost story or a lesser-known gem by Virginia Woolf – which you’ll get to take home.

Age limit: 18+

events.title: Faridah Àbíké-Íyímídé: The Heirs
events.blurb: Secrets, lies, murder, and money – all the ingredients needed for a killer read. Faridah Àbíké-Íyímídé gives us a rollercoaster of twists in her gripping thriller, The Heirs, following the five genius children of an infamous billionaire. Come along to meet and hear from the bestselling author of Ace of Spades and Where Sleeping Girls Lie, and after, you’ll get a chance to hang out with fellow readers and fans of a good murder mystery. Chaired by Eleanor Morton.

events.title: Gemma Cairney: The Immortal Sisterhood
events.blurb: Travellers have often looked to the stars for guidance; but, for award-winning broadcaster and author Gemma Cairney, her constellation is a cluster of 12 inspirational women across history. Cairney talks to us about her radiant book, The Immortal Sisterhood – full of dream-like essays that, like the boundary-breaking women who influence them, defy expectation and form. Discover Cairney’s immortal sisterhood in a conversation that’ll leave you reflecting on your own guiding stars and how they’ve shaped you. Chaired by Sarah Gwonyoma.

events.title: Samira Ahmed & Ian Leslie: Two of Us
events.blurb: They may be one of the most legendary and influential groups to have ever existed but there’s still so much to know about the Beatles. Ian Leslie’s John and Paul reframes Lennon and McCartney’s relationship like never before, while Samira Ahmed’s A Hard Day’s Night reveals how the Beatles' first film transformed the band. The pair come together today to chat about their joyous, myth-challenging biographies, offering fresh perspectives on the lads from Liverpool. Chaired by Vikki Reilly.

events.title: Pen Pals: Tash Aw & Édouard Louis
events.blurb: From the moment they met at a literary festival, Tash Aw and Édouard Louis’ friendship was intertwined with their creative processes. Aw, whose novel The South was longlisted for the 2025 Booker Prize, began a daily exchange of ideas with Louis, the depth of their understanding making him a natural choice to translate the French author’s gut-wrenchingly personal books – most recently, Collapse. They come together to discuss their friendship as a ‘laboratory for creation’. Chaired by Daniel Hahn.

events.title: Alison Irvine: Barrowland
events.blurb: Playing Glasgow’s iconic Barrowland Ballroom is a ‘Made it!’ moment for bands around the world. Acts including David Bowie, Blondie, Biffy Clyro, The Clash, and thousands more have had its sprung floors bouncing, and sweat dripping from its star-studded ceiling. There’s no other room like it in the world. Today, Barrowland author Alison Irvine takes us into its backstage corners to reveal the venue's unseen story, celebrating some of its electric gigs and demands for ‘WAN MAIR CHOON!’. Chaired by Fiona Shepherd.

events.title: Hollie McNish: Virgin
events.blurb: Virginity is something Hollie McNish has spent years thinking about, from the looming presence we can feel it has in our youth, to whether the Virgin Mary ever got annoyed by her eternal nickname. In Virgin, McNish picks at the six-letter word with her trademark mix of softness, frankness, and humour, to explore its true power. Hear the Ted Hughes Award-winning author of Lobster and Slug dive further into these thoughts and experience her electric stage presence firsthand. Chaired by Sarah Gwonyoma.

events.title: 404 Ink: Ten Years of Publishing Loudly
events.blurb: Publishing loudly was always the name of the game at alternative press 404 Ink, but all good things must come to an end. After 10 years fostering some of the country’s most exciting literary talent, innovating every step of the way, you’re invited to join co-founders Heather McDaid and Laura Jones-Rivera as they end their story not with a whimper, but a banging celebration of their brilliant authors. Featuring Genevieve Jagger, Nadine Aisha Jassat, Carrie Marshall, Elle Nash, Andrés N Ordorica, and Arusa Qureshi. (Note: this is a standing, party-style event with limited seating).

events.title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
events.blurb: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers with Vivian French.

events.title: Changemakers with Paterson Joseph & David Olusoga
events.blurb: Don’t miss this powerful session on Black British history with author, historian, broadcaster, and The Traitors' Faithful, David Olusoga and author and actor Paterson Joseph. David’s Black and British: An Illustrated History for Young Readers is jam-packed with facts, stories, and stunning pictures, while Paterson’s TEN: Children Who Changed the World introduces 10 incredible children who were born when slavery was still legal. This will be a super interesting chat about neglected histories and remarkable figures.

events.title: Tom Gates and Other Excellent Things with Liz Pichon
events.blurb: Are you ready for some serious silliness? Liz Pichon is here with the very doodly world of Tom Gates, the kid who's still just trying to work it all out. Come and meet Tom's very funny creator Liz, who's sold over 16.5 MILLION copies of her books! It's enough to cheer up Delia. Liz will also be transporting us to the Isle of Smile to meet the Mubbles, with singing, laughter and an awful lot of brilliance.

events.title: Sprog Rock
events.blurb: Returning to rock the Book Festival for the sixth year, it’s Sprog Rock! Get ready to dance at this rocking and (nursery) rhyming extravaganza, as the group brings their unique, catchy songs back to our Spiegeltent. Fun for under-fives and their grooviest grown-ups, friends, and families.

events.title: Music and Making with Wild Wings of Hope
events.blurb: Did you know there’s a bird called a swift which travels all the way from Edinburgh to Africa every year? Amazing, right? Join Wild Wings of Hope for a delightful drop in session packed with stories, papercrafts, and drumming inspired by those brilliant wee birds. With Scottish artist Ed Harrison and Ghanaian storyteller and musician Chief Gift Amu.

events.title: Football Freestyling with Ben Nuttall
events.blurb: The undisputed World Number One football freestyler (he even performs for Manchester United) and social media superstar brings us his book, Ben Nuttall’s Footy Factory! But will Ben Nuttall just be talking about his tricks? Oh no, he’ll be showing you step-by-step how to do them – and you’ll also hear the incredible stories of the famous players who performed them for real on matchday! Your mind will be BLOWN.

events.title: Skandar’s Secrets with A F Steadman
events.blurb: Ferocious unicorns, nail-biting battles, and elemental magic – expect this and more in Skandar and the Spirit War, the final instalment of A F Steadman’s epic series. The Mainland is under threat after the Chaos Cup – can Skandar become the leader he needs to be? Hear from the bestselling author as she answers your burning questions about our favourite unlikely hero, his unicorn rider friends, and what it takes to build a fantastical world.

events.title: How to Make Awesome Comics with Neill Cameron
events.blurb: The Phoenix favourite and creator of the Mega Robo Bros and Donut Squad series Neill Cameron hosts a hands on skills session to spill the secrets behind making divinely daft comics. From naming characters to framing stories and putting as much chaos into a tiny box as possible, this is a creative, cosy event for anyone who’s a fan of Sprinkles, Spronky, and the rest of the silly, sticky gang.

events.title: Music and Making with Wild Wings of Hope
events.blurb: Did you know there’s a bird called a swift which travels all the way from Edinburgh to Africa every year? Amazing, right? Join Wild Wings of Hope for a delightful drop in session packed with stories, papercrafts, and drumming inspired by those brilliant wee birds. With Scottish artist Ed Harrison and Ghanaian storyteller and musician Chief Gift Amu.

events.title: A Cupful of Kindness with Chris Naylor-Ballesteros
events.blurb: When a mysterious stranger arrives with a teacup, the animals think ‘Thief!’. But things really aren’t that simple. Be moved and mesmerised by Chris Naylor-Ballesteros’s gorgeous new picture book, The Teacup – the follow-up to his runaway success, The Suitcase. Snuggle in and stretch your imagination in this gentle event about kindness to strangers and tolerance for others who might seem different to us – an inspiring event that you’ll both love and learn from.

events.title: Sprog Rock
events.blurb: Returning to rock the Book Festival for the sixth year, it’s Sprog Rock! Get ready to dance at this rocking and (nursery) rhyming extravaganza, as the group brings their unique, catchy songs back to our Spiegeltent. Fun for under-fives and their grooviest grown-ups, friends, and families.

events.title: The Compassion Salon: Book Festival Edition
events.blurb: Compassion is at the heart of community, something which social entrepreneur, healthcare academic, and author Dr Marti Balaam has nurtured in Edinburgh since 2019 with her uplifting literary salon, celebrating literature that focuses on empathy and wellbeing. The Compassion Salon is a space for people to connect and reflect on what it is to be human. Today’s event, in partnership with Edinburgh Medical School 300, features writer and GP Gavin Francis, poet Hollie McNish, and Edinburgh’s Makar Michael Pedersen.

events.title: The Inside Scoop on Investigations
events.blurb: There is no better definition of good information than diligent, impartial, well-resourced investigative journalism, where rumours are sifted from verified facts which lead to action. Discussing this most specialised of fields are a panel including Centre for Investigative Journalism chair Isabel Hilton and Lucia Osborne-Crowley, whose acclaimed book, The Lasting Harm: Witnessing the Trial of Ghislaine Maxwell, draws on firsthand court reporting from one of the most high-profile cases in living memory.

events.title: Rebecca Birrell & Megan Hunter: Love Against the Shadows
events.blurb: In Megan Hunter’s Days of Light, an enchanted afternoon in Bloomsbury-inspired Sussex ends in a tragedy which echoes across six decades, while Rebecca Birrell’s Venus, Vanishing evokes the heady, dangerous world of 1930s Berlin. In both, beauty and risk intertwine, and queer love blazes defiantly under the shadow of loss, repression, and catastrophe. Hear major new talent Birrell, and author of The End We Start from, Hunter, discussing art, hidden histories, and the fierce, fragile force of love. Chaired by Nell Stevens.

events.title: Candice Carty-Williams: Queenie is Working on It
events.blurb: Some protagonists are so full of life, they become as real to us as friends. Candice Carty-Williams’ Queenie is among the best of them. What a treat that we get to meet her again in the much-anticipated sequel, Queenie is Working on It – 10 years older but apparently none the wiser.
