Discover the practical, scalable ways we can collectively fix our broken systems and work towards a purposeful future, together. Chaired by Benny Higgins.

events.title: Juno Dawson: Survival Show
events.blurb: Ready for the performance of your life? In Juno Dawson’s new YA novel, Survival Show, a young woman enters the most watched reality TV show in the world in order to help her family, but soon comes face to face with the work of a brutal regime. Come meet the utterly brilliant author of Clean and Her Majesty's Royal Coven and listen in to her thoughtful chat about the dangers of fame, power, and survival. Chaired by Alice Tarbuck.

events.title: Alycia Pirmohamed & Ece Temelkuran: Hope when Home is Lost [Hoda Bakarat has cancelled]
events.blurb: How does our understanding of the ideas of ‘home’ and ‘belonging’ shift in a war-torn and warming world? Today’s event features a powerful conversation with three authors writing urgently about displacement and connection: Alycia Pirmohamed (poet and winner of the Nan Shepherd Prize with non-fiction debut, Shorelines), and Ece Temelkuran (essayist and Women’s Prize for Nonfiction-shortlisted author of Nation of Strangers). Chaired by Mohamed Tonsy.

events.title: Steve Mason: Failure is Always an Option
events.blurb: Edinburgh’s Beta Band had the world at their feet, with Hollywood’s seal of approval through the film version of Nick Hornby’s High Fidelity, and praise from Noel Gallagher and Radiohead. Then it all fell apart in a blaze of self-indulgence, wrong decisions, and mental health crises. Two decades on, and with the band on tour once more, charismatic frontman Steve Mason chats about his memoir Failure is Always an Option, telling a glorious rock-underdog tale. Chaired by Nicola Meighan.

events.title: Fiona Mozley: Awake, Awake
events.blurb: When Mary begins remembering things that can’t be real, she must reconnect with friends long since scattered to reconstruct the truth. Set between the misplaced optimism of the New Labour years and the post-financial-crash 2010s, Awake Awake is the absorbing new novel from Fiona Mozley, Booker Prize-shortlisted author of the groundbreaking Elmet and Hot Stew. Hear Mozley explore the formation of identity and how the self is less stable than we'd like to believe. Chaired by Jenny Brown.

events.title: Matt Haig: The Midnight Train
events.blurb: Few authors take residence inside a reader’s heart like Matt Haig, who follows up his multi-million copy bestseller The Midnight Library with a new story set in the same world. The Midnight Train is a moving tale of time-travel, love, and adventure, which asks: which of your past mistakes would you choose to resolve if given the chance? Haig today discusses the seductive power of second chances, and the countless lives we never lived due to the choices we did – and didn’t – make. Chaired by Sophie Gee.

events.title: Five Tastes: A Table Talk with Fuchsia Dunlop
events.blurb: Fuchsia Dunlop has long been both master and student of Sichuan cuisine, and in Five Tastes – which she launches with us this evening – she breaks down exactly how to build dishes that balance sweet and salty notes. Part chef, part magician, witness (and taste) her brilliance as she walks us through the training, travel, and endless trial and error that’s earned her respect across China and beyond. Chaired by Chitra Ramaswamy. Ticket includes: a welcome drink and a delicious food taster.

events.title: Len Pennie & Paul-Leonard Morgan: Delusions
events.blurb:
This breathtaking collaboration between acclaimed poet Len Pennie and BAFTA-winning composer Paul Leonard-Morgan, which premiered at 2026’s Celtic Connections festival, blends poetry and spoken word with epic sound for a genre defying performance in the beautiful surroundings of Greyfriars Kirk. Tackling themes of love, loss, wonder, and rage, Delusions melds Pennie’s gut-punching words with Leonard-Morgan’s soaring music, performed on piano, strings, and electronica. No heart will leave unmoved. Full line-up includes Len Pennie, Paul-Leonard Morgan, Greg Lawson, Cheryl Crockett, Gordon Bragg Gordon, Bianca Wesley-Smith, Su-a Lee, Daniel Griffin.

Part of Scotland to the World. Supported by Sir Ewan and Lady Brown.

events.title: Missouri Williams: The Vivisectors
events.blurb: Missouri Williams’ work holds up a mirror to the many contradictions that make up our humanity. She captured the world’s attention with cult debut The Doloriad, a gothic tale of depravity and salvation in a postapocalyptic world, and now she’s back with The Vivisectors, a satire about a misanthropic graduate who gets tangled up in a campus conspiracy. Don’t miss this thought-provoking conversation with a writer who sees right into the darkest corners of our minds. Chaired by Barry Pierce.

events.title: Lawrence Abu Hamdan: Radical Listening
events.blurb: From his 2012 documentary, The Whole Truth, to his 2019 Turner Prize-winning installation, Walled Unwalled, visionary artist Lawrence Abu Hamdan makes use of sound to investigate that which is not seen, but heard. In 2023, he founded the organisation Earshot, dedicated to the study of audio for human rights and environmental advocacy. Today, he discusses combining the role of artist and investigator and offers an introduction to Earshot’s transformation of sound into a tool of justice. Chaired by Antonis Vradis.

events.title: Mieko Kawakami: Sisters in Yellow
events.blurb: Superstar Mieko Kawakami is one of the driving forces behind the explosion of popularity of Japanese fiction in the UK; the seven top selling translated authors in 2025 were all Japanese. Following her smash hit, Breasts and Eggs, Mieko Kawakami brings us Sisters in Yellow, a tale of friendship, betrayal, and dive bars set in the gritty alleyways of 90’s Tokyo – every bit as brilliantly unorthodox as her last novel. Presented in partnership with the award-winning ESEA Lit Fest, today’s conversation sees her chatting about it with Maria Garbutt-Lucero.

events.title: All Star Poetry
events.blurb: Pin-drop silence, riotous laughter, and back-of-the-neck goosebumps are just a few common side effects from our poetry evenings, and it doesn’t get much better than this spectacular showcase of internationally acclaimed poets. Join us for a dazzling evening of performance with poets including Brian Bilston, Rachel Long, and Michael Pedersen. Check back soon for the full line-up. This event is hosted by Janette Ayachi.

events.title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
events.blurb: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Check website for today's author.

events.title: First Edition: Equator
events.blurb: Start your day with the facts. Equator magazine is dedicated to politics, culture, and art, founded on the conviction of a small group of writers and editors that much of the Anglophone West’s media is in a state of crisis and beyond reform. Today, join the magazine’s editors, writers, and contributors, including Samanth Subramanian and Gavin Jacobson, discussing creating a new outlet for a globalised and interconnected era, and why the widely proclaimed ‘end of the West’ isn’t the end of the world. Chaired by Halla Mohieddeen.

events.title: Stranger than Fiction: A Workshop with Katie Goh
events.blurb: Kickstart your creative nonfiction writing project with Katie Goh – writer, editor, and author of Jhalak Prize-shortlisted memoir, Foreign Fruit. Explore the many innovative ways that essays, memoir, and other forms of creative nonfiction can tell a story, then get stuck into exercises that’ll leave you buzzing with ideas. All are welcome to this workshop, presented in partnership with the award-winning ESEA Lit Fest; best suited to new or emerging writers.

events.title: Gaelic Bookbug
events.blurb: Halò a h-uile duine! Join our friends from Scottish Book Trust for Gaelic songs, rhymes and stories in this special Gaelic Bookbug Session. This session will feature the books included in the Gaelic Bookbug Bags. All welcome, no prior knowledge of Gaelic language necessary!

events.title: Fresh Words: Women’s Prize Trust Discoveries
events.blurb: It’s lunchtime, but there’s no need to doomscroll over your meal deal. Be the first to discover the literary stars of the future, instead. In partnership with Scottish Book Trust and other leading UK talent spotters, this lively event showcases electrifying new voices, so grab your seat before everyone else does. Today, we partner with the Women’s Prize Trust Discoveries Award, hearing readings from an amazing line-up of writers. Women's Prize writers: Niamh Connolly, Georgia Moorhouse, Beena Nadeem, Tara O'Sullivan, Carol Farrelly and Krystelle Bamford.

events.title: Gordon Brown: The Future Starts with Us
events.blurb: In an age of global instability and civic decline, what’s gone wrong and what can ordinary people do to bring positive change to the world? As former British Prime Minister and Chancellor of the Exchequer, and a current United Nations special envoy, World Health Organisation ambassador, and special envoy on global finance to the current UK government, Gordon Brown is well-placed to answer these questions in his new book, The Future Starts with Us. Hear his reflections today in conversation with Lyse Doucet.

events.title: Scotland to the World: On Adaptation
events.blurb:
Words can create melody, rhythm, even symphonies. Our Scotland to the World series takes this a step further, pairing some of our most notable writers and acclaimed musicians to create new performances. Kate Molleson talks to Ali Smith and New European Ensemble principal artistic director Emlyn Stam as they unpack the collaboration process behind Seasonal Quartet, alongside poet Len Pennie and BAFTA Award-winning composer Paul Leonard-Morgan, who reflect on their genre-defying performance, Delusions. 

Part of Scotland to the World.

events.title: Polish Bookbug
events.blurb: Witamy Wszystkich! Czas na polską sesję ‘BookBug’! Join us for this special Polish Bookbug Session – enjoy songs, stories, and rhymes in this fun, interactive event. All welcome, no prior knowledge of the Polish language necessary. Facilitated by Kuba Stepniewski.

events.title: Sebastian Mallaby & Tim Wu: The Extraction Machine
events.blurb: Tech development continues at an unprecedented rate; how do we ensure it works for the good of humanity, not the enrichment of a few? Two authors with unique insight behind the digital curtain thrash out the problem and possible solutions with Misha Glenny. Sebastian Mallaby discusses The Infinity Machine – his biography of DeepMind founder, Demis Hassabis – and Tim Wu talks The Age of Extraction and tech monopolists’ quest to mine humanity for data, attention, intention, and profit.

events.title: Fuchsia Dunlop: The Magic of Flavour in a Chinese Kitchen
events.blurb: There aren’t many Brits who’ve immersed themselves in Chinese food culture quite like Fuchsia Dunlop – lauded as a ‘world authority’ (Observer Food Monthly) who ‘understands Chinese cuisine better than any other foreigner I know’ (food documentarian Chen Xiaoqing), Dunlop’s books bring her culinary explorations to a Western audience. Today she chats about Five Tastes: The Magic of Flavour in a Chinese Kitchen, celebrating the philosophy that good health and pleasure are inseparable when it comes to food. Chaired by Sean Wai Keung.

events.title: The Front List: Elif Shafak
events.blurb: Elif Shafak has published 21 books, including 13 acclaimed novels, and been translated into 58 languages. Following a sold out event discussing There are Rivers in the Sky in 2024, today’s special celebratory event sees Shafak – a powerful advocate for women’s and LGBTQ+ rights and freedom of speech – reflects on her rich career to date, what it means to be a truly global author and citizen, and the impact of putting her personal and political beliefs into tangible action.

events.title: Daniyal Mueenuddin: This is Where the Serpent Lives
events.blurb: An epic saga set in modern Pakistan, This Is Where the Serpent Lives is Daniyal Mueenuddin’s much-anticipated debut novel, following his acclaimed story collection, In Other Rooms, Other Wonders. The novel, shifting between the perspectives of a dozen characters, builds a compelling portrait of the feudal division of land and labour in contemporary Pakistan. Join this fascinating conversation with Mueenuddin, exploring choice and survival, caste and capital, resilience and tragedy. Chaired by Sana Goyal.

events.title: Impossible Creatures Made Real with Katherine Rundell
events.blurb: Dragons, griffins, sphinxes, centaurs – on a cluster of magical islands called the Archipelago, creatures of myth still live. Katherine Rundell’s multi-award-winning Impossible Creatures series tells the story of how an ordinary boy and a flying girl get swept up in adventures they’ll never forget. Today Katherine shares the epic third book, The Neverfear – how did she create such a richly imagined world? And what tips does she have for budding young writers with wild imaginations?

events.title: Rana Dasgupta & Ece Temelkuran: Crossing Borders
events.blurb: National borders are an increasing source of friction as many demand their security, cross them seeking refuge, invade over them, or no longer feel at home within them. Esa Aldegheri talks about these human-made faultlines with essayist Rana Dasgupta – who, in After Nations, explores the creation of modern nation states and their present turmoil – and journalist Ece Temelkuran – whose Nation of Strangers weaves an urgent tapestry of exile and displacement, asking what ‘home’ means.

events.title: How to Write the Future: A Workshop with Saleem Haddad
events.blurb: Join filmmaker and Floodlines author, Saleem Haddad, to explore how, as writers, we can imagine the future in times of turbulence and uncertainty, and how to create speculative fiction that feels both emotionally and politically resonant. Combining textual analysis, group discussion, and guided writing exercises, this workshop is suitable for writers of all levels who want to illuminate the dystopia – or utopia – into which we may be heading.

events.title: Sarah Howe, Rachel Long & Sarah Stewart: Lyric Memory
events.blurb: Poetry has the capacity to say what other forms cannot. In Sarah Howe’s Foretokens, for example, the T. S. Eliot Prize-winner forms a portrait of a mother in search of her past and herself. Sarah Stewart’s Devour Everything, meanwhile, wrestles with issues of motherhood, memory, and loss, and Rachel Long’s Sparrow on the Rooftop interrogates the experience of self as other. Join these remarkable poets discussing their new collections with Marjorie Lotfi.

events.title: Bookbug with Edinburgh Libraries
events.blurb: Hello everyone! It's time for Bookbug. Join Edinburgh Libraries for songs, stories, and rhymes in this much-loved, fun, interactive event. We heard that we might get a visit from the one and only Bookbug, so you can even get a photo, a hug, and a cheeky high-five! Part of the Scottish Book Trust's Early Years programme.

events.title: Scots Storytelling with the Scots Language Centre
events.blurb: Bring the bairns alang fir a Scots storytelling session. Abody’s welcome, whither ye ken Scots weel ir ye ir jist lairnin. It’s goin tae be braw!

events.title: House of YA x Edinburgh International Book Festival Spiegeltent Takeover
events.blurb:
House of YA is back! They’ll be taking over the Spiegeltent again this year with another selection of the hottest titles in Young Adult fiction, all wrapped in a cosy afternoon of good company. Your ticket will get you access to everything, so stay for the whole 
thing or pop in and out as much as you like. Although when you see the line-up, you won’t want to be anywhere else.

events.title: Bookbug with Edinburgh Libraries
events.blurb: Hello everyone! It's time for Bookbug. Join Edinburgh Libraries for songs, stories, and rhymes in this much-loved, fun, interactive event. We heard that we might get a visit from the one and only Bookbug, so you can even get a photo, a hug, and a cheeky high-five! Part of the Scottish Book Trust's Early Years programme.

events.blurb: Bring the bairns alang fir a Scots storytelling session. Abody’s welcome, whither ye ken Scots weel ir ye ir jist lairnin. It’s goin tae be braw!

events.title: Fatima Bhutto & Ayşegül Savaş: Who Am I Now?
events.blurb: Some life events are so all-consuming that they melt you down and remake you anew. For the writer and columnist Fatima Bhutto, it was leaving the coercive relationship she writes about in The Hour of the Wolf that helped her feel solid again. She joins The Anthropologists author Ayşegül Savaş, who details the destabilising impact of motherhood in The Wilderness, for a radically honest conversation about how they came back to themselves. Chaired by Octavia Bright.

events.title: Colm Tóibín: The News from Dublin
events.blurb: Colm Tóibín – author of 12 books including the multi-award-winning Brooklyn – is one of modern Ireland’s greatest writers. He talks with Chris Power about his breathtaking new story collection, The News from Dublin, exploring the lives of those living far from home: from Galway to Barcelona, Enniscorthy to San Francisco, and beyond. This promises to be an illuminating conversation with a true master of the craft.

events.title: Writing the Darkness with Patrick Ness
events.blurb: Patrick Ness is a titan of Young Adult literature. Author of modern classic, The Knife of Never Letting Go, he returns to the world of the bestselling Chaos Walking trilogy with Piper at the Gates of Dusk. Blending sci-fi, speculative fiction, and adventure, it’s a story of power, division, and hope. Hear Patrick talk about going back to a world he created nearly 20 years ago and what it takes to write award-winning science fiction.

events.title: Molly Crabapple: Here Where We Live Is Our Country
events.blurb: Here Where We Live Is Our Country tells the story of the Jewish Bund, a revolutionary movement not given enough space in recorded history – until now. Molly Crabapple draws on the lives of 20th-century rebels – including her own great-grandfather – who stood up to the Tsar, the Nazis, and ethnonationalists in the name of freedom. A New York Times bestseller and praised by the likes of Naomi Klein and Angela Davis, we can’t wait to hear her brilliance live and direct. Chaired by Seth Anziska.

events.title: Angela Flournoy & Agnes Lidbeck: Love and Politics
events.blurb: We’ve all felt relationships changing shape as they’re buffeted by external winds, but none have written about this quite as beautifully as Angela Flournoy and Agnes Lidbeck. The authors join forces today to discuss this thread running through their novels. In The Wilderness, four women weather the storms of rising conservatism and new motherhood, while All My Love follows two couples who find their desires shifting with the political currents. Chaired by Sam Baker.

events.title: Sally Hayden & Roxani Krystalli: War and Peace
events.blurb: In This is Also a Love Story, Sally Hayden – Orwell Prize-winning journalist and author of My Fourth Time, We Drowned – offers a staggering account of human kindness against the backdrop of global crises. As both an academic and humanitarian, Roxani Krystalli works at the intersection of gender and peacebuilding, examining the role of love and care in remaking worlds after loss. They discuss with Esa Aldegheri what sustains life in the face of crises and what’s needed to create a better world.

events.title: Maria Stepanova: The Disappearing Act
events.blurb: Severed from her homeland and language, the exiled writer at the centre of The Disappearing Act has a lot in common with her creator, Maria Stepanova. This dreamlike meditation on Russian guilt, tainted identity, and starting over asks whether it is ever really possible to begin again. One of Russia's greatest living writers, the author of In Memory of Memory explores what remains when home becomes the enemy. Chaired by Chris Power.

events.title: Tareq Baconi & Saleem Haddad: Fire and Flood
events.blurb: Both Tareq Baconi’s Fire in Every Direction and Saleem Haddad’s Floodlines consider the generational impacts of family myths and global conflicts – the former through an intimate memoir, and the latter through a fictional tale influenced by his family stories. Examining queerness, art, displacement, and the relationship between the Middle East and UK, join them for a thoughtful and personal discussion about memories, estrangement, reconnection, and the meaning of home. Chaired by Mohamed Tonsy.

events.title: Katy Hessel: How to Live an Artful Life
events.blurb: As modern life pulls our attention in every direction, how can we carve space for our creative lives? Katy Hessel has a few ideas – 365 to be exact. After years dedicated to spotlighting the Great Women Artists, the historian, podcaster, and bestselling author of The Story of Art Without Men, joins Octavia Bright to share How to Live an Artful Life: a year-full of inspiration to help us all slow down and view the world anew.

events.title: Eyal Weizman: Ungrounding
events.blurb: Director of the organisation Forensic Architecture, Eyal Weizman is a world-leading expert on the relationship between conflict and the built and natural environments. Since 2023, the group has worked to produce evidence for the International Court of Justice’s genocide case against Israel, using architectural and territorial analysis. In Ungrounding, he unveils a chilling insider’s view of the history and 'deep cartography' of the war, unflinchingly cataloging the campaigns of violence and displacement that have reshaped Gaza. Join him for an eye-opening discussion on how the new interdisciplinary field of forensic architecture is used to uncover the truth. Chaired by Leonie Bell.

events.title: Seasonal Quartet: New European Ensemble & Ali Smith
events.blurb:
Ali Smith’s evocative Seasonal Quartet novels are brought to life anew in this special collaboration with Netherlands’ New European Ensemble (NEuE). Four female composers have created new musical works inspired by the series’ themes of interconnectedness, migration, and our place in a troubled world. Experience an unforgettable performance blending new commissions from leading European musicians with moving readings from the author herself. Full line-up includes Ali Smith, Felicia van den End, James Meldrum, Hanna Shybayeva, Rada Ovcharova, Alva Holm, Emlyn Stam and Willem Stam.
Part of Scotland to the World.

events.title: Hélène Giannecchini & Joelle Taylor: Chosen Families
events.blurb: Joelle Taylor (Maryville, C+nto & Othered Poems) and Hélène Giannecchini (An Army of Lovers Cannot Fail) consider the political power and potential of queer kinship, each resisting the notion that friendships are second to romantic and family relationships. Through poetry and creative non-fiction, and by mixing personal history, imagination, and archival research, Taylor and Giannecchini’s work promises a lively conversation on what sustains queer life, from solidarity to resistance, grief to joy. Chaired by Sasha de Buyl.

events.title: Meg Mason: Sophie, Standing There (THIS EVENT IS TAKING PLACE IN VENUE NW)
events.blurb: Meg Mason wrang our hearts with her wit and compassion in Sorrow and Bliss. Now she follows that Women’s Prize-shortlisted success with her darkly humorous new novel, Sophie, Standing There, following a book festival employee who becomes obsessed with a star writer. Join Cathy Rentzenbrink today as she chats with Mason about loneliness and laughter, the peculiar power of literary festivals, and whether a person can really read themselves better.

events.title: Caledonia Screaming: 50 Years of Punk
events.blurb: Hey! Ho! Let's Go! It’s been 50 years since the first punk gig in Scotland so we’re throwing a suitably anarchic bash to celebrate. Grant McPhee gives us the lowdown via his oral history of Scottish punk, Caledonia Screaming. Then we’re thrilled to welcome a specially formed supergroup including legends Alex Fergusson (Alternative TV/Psychic TV), Ken McCluskey (The Bluebells), and James King (James King and the Lonewolves) for an electric performance! Chaired by Nicola Meighan. This event's house band features Douglas MacIntyre, Mick Slaven, Campbell Owens and Stuart Kidd.

events.title: Relaxed Screening: The Wonderful World of Julia Donaldson
events.blurb: Some of us thrive better in smaller, informal spaces. That’s why we’re putting on this relaxed screening for anyone with sensory sensitivities. You can watch the livestream of ‘The Wonderful World of Julia Donaldson’ while being able to move around, come and go, and make noise in this friendly, chilled out space.

events.title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
events.blurb: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Check website for today's author.

events.title: Mike Gayle: On We Go
events.blurb: Since the late 90s, Mike Gayle has written ordinary characters dealing with everyday chaos with humour, romance, and grace: from life after university (My Legendary Girlfriend), to mid-twenties relationships (Mr Commitment) and the reality of moving back in with parents (Turning Thirty). His latest novel, On We Go, is about grief, awkward reunions, and even awkwarder holidays. Hear Gayle delve into the twists, turns, and tempers that only a trip with your extended family can bring. Chaired by Bryan Burnett.

events.title: The Wonderful World of Julia Donaldson
events.blurb: It's Julia Donaldson time! Join the UK’s bestselling author of stories like The Gruffalo, Room on the Broom, and A Squash and a Squeeze for a fun-packed hour of songs, poems, and stories, featuring lots of your family’s favourite characters. Prepare your singing voices and get ready to boogie – it’s going to be great!

events.title: Saira Hameed & Madeleine Pownall: The Gender Health Gap
events.blurb: Women have long made significant contributions to our understanding of psychology and health, yet gender inequality in research and practice remains. Saira Hameed’s Signals: The Inside Story of Our Hormones addresses common misconceptions about health and hormones, while Dr Madeleine Pownall’s Absent Minds: The Untold Story of the Women Who Changed Psychology Forever uncovers lost legacies of female psychologists who radically shaped the field. Hear this formidable duo talking today about righting wrongs. Chaired by Devi Sridhar.

events.title: Poetry and Beyond: A Workshop with Joelle Taylor
events.blurb: Ever wondered where a poem could go when it leaves the page? Join T. S. Eliot Prize-winning poet, author, and playwright Joelle Taylor to explore what new shapes poems can take on, whether they expand into novels, transform into short films, or stretch into dance. With writing exercises throughout, participants will experiment with different forms, considering which elements make each distinct, and which most fire their imagination. Suitable for everyone willing to play and take risks.

events.title: Looking at Art Again with Katy Hessel
events.blurb: Sometimes, it can look like the only people who ever made art were men. But the author of The Story of Art Without Men, Katy Hessel, knows different – and she's here to tell you about extraordinary, rebellious, game-changing women artists, and the amazing art they created. You'll learn how to read hidden messages and find stories secretly buried in paintings. Art will never look the same again!

events.title: Fire-Breathing Facts with David Macphail
events.blurb: Get ready for a dragon-tastic tour of a very cool castle! Blaze the Dragon will be your guide, as you step back in time in David Macphail’s new book, Where’s Dragon in His Castle? With dungeons, jousting, and turrets to explore, you’ll discover incredible facts about the Middle Ages. And because David’s a real-life castle steward, he’s bringing cartloads of medieval activities for you to enjoy. It’s the funnest, friendliest introduction to history ever.

events.title: Meet the Gruffalo
events.blurb: Oh help! Oh no! It’s the Gruffalo! But don’t worry, he’s incredibly friendly and can’t wait to meet you! Come along for a photo and a cuddle while he’s visiting from the deep dark wood.

events.title: Dogs and Bears and Brilliant Fun! With Max Porter and Dorothée de Monfreid
events.blurb:
Get ready to bark, growl, and roar with laughter! Step into a wonderfully wild storytelling adventure with award-winning, bestselling author Max Porter and illustrator Dorothée de Monfreid, in a high-energy family event about their new picture book, DOGS AND BEARS. Find out whether you're Team Dog or Team Bear in this lively session packed with interactive games, drawing, quizzes, and pure fun! Create your own Dogs and Bears dance moves and silly songs in a live performance. 
 
Perfect for families of all ages, squids, and all other peaceful creatures.

events.title: Ali Smith: Glyph
events.blurb: For Scotland's own beloved Ali Smith, words are never neutral – they are alive, exuberant, political. Glyph, a dazzling companion to last year's Gliff, is a powerful yet playful anti-war novel set in a state turned hostile to curiosity and understanding. She returns to the Festival today to celebrate stories within stories, language as resistance, and the power of words to confront dark times and and help us see other perspectives. Chaired by Claire Armitstead.

events.title: A Birthday Party for… Charlie and Lola
events.blurb: Mark your calendars, dust off your dancing shoes, and get ready to party! Loads of our favourite books have big anniversaries this year so we’re throwing some of them a special birthday bash. Come along today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Lauren Child’s wonderful, whimsical series, Charlie and Lola. There’ll be storytime, party games, dancing, and singing (and absolutely NO tomatoes!) as we wish everyone’s favourite siblings many happy returns.

events.title: Future Library
events.blurb: Norway’s Future Library is a powerful gesture of hope for a world beyond our lifetime. Created by Scottish artist Katie Paterson in 2014, every year, for 100 years, an author writes a new text to be placed inside the library. Every text remains unread until 2114. Join Paterson and Future Library’s Anne Beate Hovind talking about the remarkable project with previous contributors Elif Shafak and Valeria Luiselli, then be first to find out the sensational new writer contributing to the Future Library in 2027.

events.title: Ian Patterson & Cathy Rentzenbrink: Reading Remedies
events.blurb: We suspect that telling you about the radical importance of reading is a bit preach-to-the-choir. Humour us though, as poet and translator Ian Patterson (Books - A Manifesto) encourages reading past your comfort zone – adding avant-garde poems or a bonkbuster to your shelves, perhaps. He’s joined by journalist and bestseller Cathy Rentzenbrink who, in The Agatha Cure, looks through Christie’s canon, asking: who are books for, why do we read, and why do we sometimes stop? Chaired by Jonty Claypole.

events.title: Meet the Gruffalo
events.blurb: Oh help! Oh no! It’s the Gruffalo! But don’t worry, he’s incredibly friendly and can’t wait to meet you! Come along for a photo and a cuddle while he’s visiting from the deep dark wood.

events.title: The Front List: Ann Patchett
events.blurb: Ann Patchett is one of the most masterful and beloved writers of our time. Her new novel, Whistler, is a radiant story about the power of human connection to defy time, as a woman unexpectedly encounters her former stepfather years after a brief but life-shaping bond. In this unmissable conversation, the incomparable cartographer of human emotion, and author of Bel Canto and The Dutch House, reflects on memory, belonging, and a literary life devoted to exploring what makes us who we are.

events.title: Have Lunch with Dara Klein
events.blurb: Raised in her parents’ restaurant, Dara Klein could layer lasagna with her eyes closed. With the flair for family-style Puglian cooking in her blood, she's just launched London’s buzziest new eatery, Tiella. We’re thrilled to have this top chef with us, fresh from writing La Trattoria, to cook up an exceptional Italian lunch and share the skills she’s been sharpening since childhood. Ticket includes: a welcome drink, a generous multi-course lunch, and paired wine on the table.

events.title: Sunshine is Guaranteed with Alex Milway
events.blurb: All aboard the sunshine cruise on a ship bursting with animals! It's Captain Bella's first day commanding the Sunshine, but it's no easy task for her and the crew. With entertaining penguins and brave seadogs to lend a hand, do they have what it takes? In this charming event with Alex Milway, bestselling author-illustrator of Hotel Flamingo, set sail on an enchanting voyage around friendship and teamwork with his terrific new book, Captain Sunshine.

events.title: Y M Abdel-Magied, Molly Crabapple & Hannah Lilith Assadi: Global Solidarities
events.blurb: What shapes can solidarities take in these times we live in? Join Sana Goyal, editor and publishing director of Wasafiri, for a conversation on connection and public and private revolutions with Y M Abdel-Magied, whose novel At Sea offers a searing takedown of Big Oil; Molly Crabapple, who tells the story of the Jewish Bund movement in Here Where We Live Is Our Country; and Hannah Lillith Assadi, whose Paradiso 17 is loosely based on her father’s exile from Palestine after the Nakba. This event is presented in partnership with Wasafiri.

events.title: A Seriously Epic Conversation with Katie Kirby
events.blurb: Come see writer, illustrator, and inventor of the properly hilarious world of Lottie Brooks, Katie Kirby, as she spills the beans on book number nine, The Seriously Epic Holiday of Lottie Brooks. This time, Lottie’s going skiing – what could possibly go wrong? A brilliantly fun, feel-good event that’ll show you how you’re not the only one going through extremely embarrassing, mega-complicated, totally disastrous, completely chaotic, or majorly awkward moments.

events.title: Meet the Gruffalo
events.blurb: Oh help! Oh no! It’s the Gruffalo! But don’t worry, he’s incredibly friendly and can’t wait to meet you! Come along for a photo and a cuddle while he’s visiting from the deep dark wood.

events.title: Sally Magnusson: The Shapeshifter’s Daughter
events.blurb: As the host of Reporting Scotland, Sally Magnusson became known as one of our most trusted journalists – now she’s also a beloved (and bestselling!) author. Join her as she unpacks her latest novel, The Shapeshifter’s Daughter - a feminist retelling of a Norse myth set against the ancient landscapes of Orkney. How did personal history inspire this otherworldly yet utterly human exploration of father-daughter relationships, doomed love, and reclaiming identity? Chaired by Hannah McGill.

events.title: The True Power of Story: A Novel Workshop with John Yorke
events.blurb: If you’ve always wanted to write a novel but are struggling to structure your work, make your ideas leap off the page, or even just get started, then join John Yorke – the UK’s foremost narrative expert, founder of the BBC Writers Academy, and author of acclaimed craft books including Into the Woods and Trip to the Moon – for this masterclass on the principles of story structure, where they come from, and why they exist.

events.title: Holly Pester & Anthony Tao: A Place Like No Other
events.blurb: In her latest collection, Cafés, Holly Pester considers how, despite its ‘normalness’, a café remakes itself through the people who pass through it. Anthony Tao’s We Met in Beijing, meanwhile, interrogates the profound sense of place that exists in a city of such multitudes. Join the poets for a thought-provoking discussion on writing around physical spaces, community centre points, and the people who inhabit cross-sections of society. Chaired by Samuel Tongue.

events.title: Queerly Beloved
events.blurb: We’re gathered here today, under the canvas of the Spiegeltent, to celebrate queer lives, voices, and literature. Hear from a lively panel of queer writers – including author and activist Tareq Baconi (Fire in Every Direction), poet Joelle Taylor (Maryville), and novelist Sara Torres (X is Where I Am) – sharing the art that’s inspired them, the stories they wish they’d found sooner, and why it matters to see your experiences represented in the culture you consume. Q Mannivanan and Sigrid Nielson (Lavender Menace co-founder) also joins this event. Check back soon for the full line-up. Chaired by Steph Harmon.

events.title: Meet the Gruffalo
events.blurb: Oh help! Oh no! It’s the Gruffalo! But don’t worry, he’s incredibly friendly and can’t wait to meet you! Come along for a photo and a cuddle while he’s visiting from the deep dark wood.

events.title: Rhyme After Rhyme with Joseph Coelho & Shirley Hottier
events.blurb: Poems can be about anything – messages in bottles or travelling to the centre of the Earth – and they are really fun to read out loud. Poet and former Waterstones Children’s Laureate Joseph Coelho is here today to do just that. He’s got loads of poems in his new book, Rapunzel is a Lettuce, and he’ll be joined by illustrator Shirley Hottier, who’ll show you how she’s turned them into beautiful pictures. See you there!

events.title: Sarah Wang: New Skin
events.blurb: In her incisive debut, New Skin, Sarah Wang mixes a heady cocktail of unattainable beauty standards, assimilation, and the poison of the American dream with a splash of body horror. Setting a mother-daughter relationship in its sights and a lot of botched plastic surgery, fans of 2024’s cult favourite The Substance will love this genre-busting ride of a book. Colm Tóibín calls the novel ‘intense, engaging, original, and hilarious’ – join him in conversation with Wang today.

events.title: Philippe Sands: 10 Years of East West Street
events.blurb: From Gaza to Ukraine to America and beyond, the rule-bound international legal order appears to be collapsing. Yet, as lawyer and author Philippe Sands argued in the Guardian recently, ‘the assault on international rules has been more or less continual since 1945’. 10 years on from East West Street – his landmark, Baillie Gifford Prize-winning family memoir uncovering the origin of the concept of genocide – Sands reflects on the ongoing defence of international law against its enemies. Chaired by Stephen Gethins.

events.title: Tim Wu: The Age of Extraction
events.blurb: Professor at Columbia Law School, special assistant to President Biden for technology and competition policy, and inventor of the term ‘net neutrality’ – Tim Wu’s work places him at the cutting edge of legal and ethical questions about the new information age. Joining us with The Age of Extraction, he breaks down the accelerating quest to extract data, attention, and profit from us, as well as how to break the tech monopoly and bring prosperity for all. Chaired by Malcolm Borthwick.

events.title: The Secret Life of Books – Live
events.blurb: In this riotous and revelatory live recording of their hit Secret Life of Books podcast, Sophie Gee and Jonty Claypole welcome Women’s Prize Award-winning author of Hamnet and Land, Maggie O’Farrell, and Durham University’s Professor of Psychology, who heads up the ReaderBank study, Ben Alderson-Day, to talk all things books, brains, and imaginations. Expect a quick-witted conversation about what on Earth is going on in our heads when we read (and write) books!

events.title: Isabel Waidner: Seeing Double
events.blurb: Things aren’t always what they seem in Isabel Waidner’s surreal, inventive work. As If, Waidner’s latest novel, following the Goldsmiths Prize-winning Sterling Karat Gold, sees two men with lives that mirror each other’s test the theory of whether it’s ever possible to choose a different path. Hear Waidner talking about this surprising, slyly poignant book and reflecting on grief, loss, ambition, and the choices we make. Chaired by Chris Power.

events.title: Sketching for Stories: An Illustration Session with Tita Berredo
events.blurb: What makes a drawing into an illustration? Find out in this encouraging skills session with artist Tita Berredo who’ll help you figure out how to turn all those brilliant ideas you have into powerful illustrations you can be proud of. Spend a relaxing hour in your arty headspace and see where inspiration can take you. Presented by SCBWI Scotland.

events.title: Valeria Luiselli & Sara Torres: The Trouble with Beginnings
events.blurb: A mother and daughter on the road in Sicily. A young woman in Barcelona caught between a dying mother and a new lover. In Valeria Luiselli's Beginning Middle End and Sara Torres' X is Where I Am, family dynamics loom large as women navigate love, grief, and starting over. Together, Luiselli (author of Lost Children Archive) and Torres (a bold new voice in Spanish literature) explore origins, memory, and the stories that shape a life. Chaired by Octavia Bright.

events.title: Pen Pals: Meg Mason & Ann Patchett
events.blurb: You’ll know Meg Mason for her poetically funny Sorrow and Bliss and Sophie, Standing There. You’ll know Ann Patchett for her dazzling Bel Canto, The Dutch House, and this year’s Whistler. What you might not know is that a deep friendship blossomed between them when a professional email turned into daily voice notes about life, death, and creativity. Listen in as the novelists unpack their one-of-a-kind connection and how it’s inspired each of them in profound ways.

events.title: Fatima Bhutto: Gaza – The Story of a Genocide
events.blurb: Edited by Fatima Bhutto and Sonia Faleiro, Gaza: The Story of a Genocide is an urgent, powerful collection of personal testimony, poetry, art, and frontline reportage, bearing witness to the vast, ongoing destruction in­flicted on Palestine. Today, Bhutto is joined by some of the collection’s award-winning contributors, including writer and activist Tareq Baconi, to reflect on their pieces and experiences, the horror of existing under current conditions, and what future lies ahead for the Palestinian people. Check back soon for the full line-up.

events.title: Joelle Taylor: Maryville
events.blurb: Joelle Taylor, the luminous T. S. Eliot and Polari Prize-winning author of C+nto & Othered Poems, brings her raucous storytelling back to Edinburgh for another knockout event. Delve into her remarkable new collection, Maryville, an innovative history-in-poems of lesbian culture and LGBTQ+ rights, told through the lens of an imagined dyke bar in London and the four butch lesbians that inhabit it. Don’t miss the riotous energy tonight as Taylor chats about and performs from the collection! Chaired by Caro Clarke.

events.title: Helle Helle & Vigdis Hjorth: Ordinary Miracles
events.blurb: Two heavyweights of Nordic fiction meet on stage for a sparky conversation with Sophie Gee about daily life as rich material. Helle Helle is a household name in Denmark, where her striking novels about ordinary people (This Should be Written in the Present Tense, they) have won every major prize. She’s joined by Norway’s Vigdis Hjorth (Is Mother Dead, Repetition), known for her sharp wit and the sort of unflinching autofiction that occasionally gets her into trouble.

events.title: Tareq Baconi & Ilan Pappé: Restorative Justice
events.blurb: Despite the ‘ceasefire’, the war in the Palestinian Occupied Territories has continued with impunity. Palestinian activist, scholar, and author of Hamas Contained: A History of Palestinian Resistance, Tareq Baconi, joins British-Israeli ‘new historian’, Ilan Pappé (Israel on the Brink), who argues that Israel’s greatest threat is now not external forces, but itself. They reflect on how the latest phase of the conflict has developed, the complicated evolution of Hamas, and what steps need to be taken for restorative justice and reconciliation. Chaired by Esa Aldegheri.

events.title: Karan Mahajan & Omar Musa: Exploring Legacies
events.blurb: Karan Mahajan and Omar Musa have produced poetry, personal essays, and hip-hop albums between them, but today their fiercely creative minds meet to discuss the familial threads connecting their novels. In Musa’s Fierceland, winner of Australia’s Victorian Premier's Prize for Fiction, siblings return to Malaysian Borneo in the wake of their father’s death, while The Complex by Mahajan (author of The Association of Small Bombs) follows a political dynasty in Delhi. Chaired by Sana Goyal.

events.title: Xiao Hai: Adrift in the South
events.blurb: China's migrant workers’ literature movement has seen a boom in recent years, with fascinating autobiographical works produced by writers involved in the nation’s gig and service economy. Xiao Hai’s Adrift in the South is a landmark memoir in this movement, offering a first-hand account of a decade spent moving between cities and factory jobs. Today, the essayist and poet provides a rare perspective on survival, dignity, and the human cost of the country's economic rise. Chaired by Anthony Tao.

events.title: Hannah Lillith Assadi: Paradiso 17
events.blurb: Hannah Lillith Assadi began writing the 2026 Women’s Prize-longlisted Paradiso 17 – a sweeping tale of an exiled Palestinian searching for home – in the final days of her father’s life. With it, she hoped to disprove a worry he’d whispered on his deathbed: that his life had been wasted. Hear Assadi speak from the heart about writing through grief to complete her powerful tribute to immigrant tenacity and the connections that endure across continents. Chaired by Anahit Behrooz.

events.title: Ben Lerner: Transcription
events.blurb: What can fiction record that our devices can’t? In Ben Lerner’s Transcription, a novelist arrives to interview his aging mentor, then drops his phone (i.e. his only recording device) in the sink. What unfolds is a searching meditation on human connection and the strange ways technology reshapes our memories. The acclaimed poet and author of The Topeka School and Leaving the Atocha Station reflects with Max Porter on memory, parenthood, and relationships.

events.title: Michael Pedersen and Friends
events.blurb: Get ready for a glorious, riotous, chat-show style evening, hosted by one of Scotland’s best-loved poets and novelists, the Edinburgh Makar himself, Michael Pedersen (Muckle Flugga). Listen in to his wonderfully winding conversations with special guests including authors Douglas Stuart (Booker Prize-winning author of Shuggie Bain, Young Mungo, and John of John), Gordon Buchanan (In the Hide) and poet and singer-songwriter Iona Zajac (who’ll bring us a few tunes!). This will be a real Festival highlight. Check back soon for the full line-up.

events.title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
events.blurb: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Check website for today's author.

events.title: In Stitches with Guy Bass
events.blurb: If you’re into spooky stuff and having a good laugh, this is the perfect event for you. Author Guy Bass invites you inside his weird and wonderful Stitch Head world – now a super cool film starring Asa Butterfield and Fern Brady. This fast and funny event reveals how Guy dreamed up his stories about the young boy who’s a mad professor’s forgotten creation. Full of ghoulish giggles, and a chance to explore the excitement of books and writing.

events.title: When Chaos Comes Calling with Louie Stowell
events.blurb: Something’s up in Midgard and it’s down to our favourite trickster to figure it out. Louie Stowell returns with her wildly popular Loki series following the mighty god who, after getting banished by Odin for bad behaviour, is forced to live on Earth as an 11-year-old boy. In this laugh-out-loud event, Louie introduces Loki: A Bad God's Guide to Causing Chaos. Dress as Thor at your own risk!

events.title: Octopus Antics with Alastair Chisholm
events.blurb: Ker-splash! Sylvester the Octopus invites you to dive into the cheekiest counting book ever! Alastair Chisholm’s fantastic new picture book, One Cheeky Octopus, is full of fishy foolishness as Sylvester uses his tentacles to nab and grab his friends’ games and toys… and even their false teeth! In this wonderfully welcoming event for wee ones, you can count on plenty of opportunities to join in. And as Sylvester learns about sharing, we can all learn our 1-2-3s.

events.title: Pen Pals: Jenny Colgan & Mike Gayle
events.blurb: The friendship between novelists Jenny Colgan and Mike Gayle constantly yields inspiration and cup-filling conversations. When they met in 2000, Colgan was an unpublished hopeful drawn to Gayle’s first novel, My Legendary Girlfriend, and their mutual reverence for romance. Since then, she’s sold 15 million books and he’s won the Romantic Novelists’ Association Outstanding Achievement Award. Today, they chat about the importance of friends who not only understand your craft but have your back. Chaired by Claire Urquhart.

events.title: Nature Journaling: A Workshop with J C Niala
events.blurb: J C Niala (The New Eden) is an award-winning writer, environmental historian, and anthropologist specialising in human-nature interactions; today, she leads an inspiring workshop for anyone curious about starting – or developing – a nature journaling practice. You’ll start with the senses and explore ways into creatively recording your relationship with the natural world. Then, under Niala’s expert guidance, you’ll experiment with creative approaches to celebrating the many forms 'nature' takes – in landscapes, cities, and our own lives.

events.title: Julian Baggini: The Book of Coffee
events.blurb: What does coffee mean to you? Perhaps it’s fuel, a morning ritual, a grounding moment of mindfulness. In The Book of Coffee, philosopher Julian Baggini (How the World Eats), dives into the steamy depths to uncover how coffee worked its way into the fabric of our culture and what it can teach us about living. Join him for a talk and tasting (hosted by Edinburgh roasters Santu Coffee) that’ll leave you feeling more alive - and alert - than ever.

events.title: Parade Prep!
events.blurb: We’ll create colourful crafts to wear, hold, and wave in our afternoon session (think rainbows, confetti, and streamers). It’s a whole family affair, and no one is too young (or old) to come together to celebrate community, joy, and the end of another fantastic Book Festival!

events.title: Funny Bunnies with Philip Ardagh
events.blurb: 3… 2…1… blast into space with some very funny bunnies! Hop along to this cosmicly funny event with Philip Ardagh, author of over 100 books (!) including Bunnies in a Rocket, the latest adventure featuring the Sunny Town Bunnies. This time they’re heading for the moon, but what will they find when they get there? Carrot-shaped aliens for sure! Buckle up for a properly goofy event – the silliness will be out of this world.

events.title: André Aciman: Stowaways
events.blurb: Global bestseller Call Me by Your Name showed us André Aciman’s gift for crafting delicately heartbreaking love stories. We're thrilled he’s back, and this time he's asking the tantalising question: what might have been? Stowaways follows happily married Julian as his world is upended by a flash drive revealing a whole, hidden life. Aciman joins us for a conversation about forks in the road and regrets that reach through the decades. Chaired by Jonty Claypole.

events.title: Major Doodle Alert with Sarah Bowie
events.blurb: Can you honestly think of anything better than drawing with someone who draws for a job!? Do just that today with Sarah Bowie who draws and writes about characters like Nina Peanut and Megan BUMFACE, including Nina’s latest outing, Major Drama Alert! Come and doodle with Sarah as she chats about Nina: amazing frozen-pizza chef, ghost hunter, mystery solver, jet-setter, creative genius, and drama queen. Maybe you’ll leave with your own graphic novel idea!

events.title: Anthony Seldon: The Brexit Effect
events.blurb: 10 years after the Brexit referendum turned British politics on its head, the culture war ignited by our exit from the European Union continues to blaze. Why did the referendum happen? What effects has it had? And what does our future outside of an embattled Europe hold? Today, Anthony Seldon – respected author, historian, biographer of eight Prime Ministers, and editor of the recent The Brexit Effect, 2016-2026 – reckons with the legacy of this historic, divisive event. Chaired by Brian Taylor.

events.title: Zakia Sewell & Rebecca Tamás: The Rituals We Share
events.blurb: Ancient traditions and folk culture can offer up unique ways to craft our own forms of meaning and connection. Writer and NTS Radio host Zakia Sewell’s Finding Albion questions whether today's new folk revival could unite our increasingly divided country, while Rebecca Tamás’ The Book of Mysteries interrogates how traditional practices can transform our relationship to nature and time. In this enlightening conversation, both authors explore their meditations on the nation’s folklore. Chaired by Jean Menzies.

events.title: The Front List: Douglas Stuart
events.blurb: With his debut novel, Shuggie Bain, Douglas Stuart created a Scottish publishing sensation and seized the 2020 Booker Prize. His hotly anticipated new work, John of John (described by Lauren Groff as ‘a fierce, glorious sting of a novel'), follows art school graduate Cal as he returns home to the Isle of Harris, tripping straight back into the old life he thought he’d burst beyond. Join Stuart for this rare and special event: an insightful exploration of the grip of family and religion, the fragility of community, and the alternating beauty and bleakness of island life.

events.title: Have Lunch with Yasmin Khan
events.blurb: Yasmin Khan’s Irani-Pakistani heritage deeply informs her cooking, from the vegetable-rich, flavour-forward recipes she’s famous for to the important daily ritual of a communal meal. Today the broadcaster and award-winning author of travel cookbooks Zaitoun, Ripe Figs, and Sabzi gathers us around the table to pass stories and brimming platters of her lovingly-made food between us. Ticket includes: a welcome drink, a generous multi-course lunch, and paired wine on the table.

events.title: Relaxed Screening: Dragons, Vikings, and Enemy Ships with Cressida Cowell
events.blurb: Some of us thrive better in smaller, informal spaces. That’s why we’re putting on this relaxed screening for anyone with sensory sensitivities. You can watch the livestream of ‘Dragons, Vikings, and Enemy Ships with Cressida Cowell’ while being able to move around, come and go, and make noise in this friendly, chilled out space.

events.title: Elizabeth McCracken: A Long Game
events.blurb: Write what you know. Never miss a day. Kill your darlings. Elizabeth McCracken is having none of it. In A Long Game, the Guggenheim Fellow, National Book Award finalist, and much-loved teacher dismantles the tired rules of fiction – from punctuation to plot – with wit, warmth, and a glorious streak of crankiness. Today, she reflects on doubt, discipline, and why the writing life is less about mastery than defending the strange, singular work only you can make. Chaired by Dan Richards.

events.title: Dragons, Vikings, and Enemy Ships with Cressida Cowell
events.blurb: Calling all dragon pals and adventurers! Hiccup Horrendous Haddock the Third and his dragons, Toothless and Windwalker, are back for another escapade at the Isle of Berk's Training School. Cressida Cowell, author and illustrator of the globally bestselling How to Train Your Dragon series, joins us with new spin-off book, How to Train Your Dragon School: Fight of the Flamestrike: Book 2. Expect a fun-filled event as Cressida chats Viking heroes and mysterious vessels.

events.title: Javier Cercas: The Anatomy of a Moment
events.blurb: February 1981. Shots ring out in Spain’s parliament. Cameras keep rolling. In The Anatomy of a Moment, one of Spain’s most important books of the past 50 years, Javier Cercas revisited the only coup ever captured live on film, transforming the footage into a forensic, gripping narrative. Now, on the 45th anniversary of its inciting event, he reflects on using a novelist’s tools to interrogate a nation’s defining crisis and reveal its very soul. Chaired by Chris Power.

events.title: Junk Journaling: A Workshop with Rachel Hazell
events.blurb: Explore the Festival’s overarching Changing Your Mind theme through the art of junk journaling: transforming discarded ephemera into beautiful books. With bookbinder Rachel Hazell, engage in mindful making through collage and chat through the many benefits (neurological and otherwise) of creative, repetitive tasks like book making. Materials are provided, though you’re invited to bring your own ‘found handwriting’ (old shopping lists, birthday cards, etc) to work with.

events.title: Victoria Bennett: The Apothecary by the Sea
events.blurb: With the years of early motherhood behind her, Victoria Bennett uprooted her family and moved from Cumbria 500 miles north to Orkney, where she set about transforming a scrappy backyard into a wild seaside garden. From teas and tinctures to tides and storms, this nourishing conversation with the award-winning author of All My Wild Mothers will explore the restorative power of growing found in her latest memoir, The Apothecary by the Sea. Chaired by Alice Tarbuck.

events.title: Put Your Records on with Corinne Bailey Rae
events.blurb: Whatever emotion you’re feeling (or want to feel), there’s a song out there for it. That’s what much loved singer-songwriter Corinne Bailey Rae explores in her charming new picture book, Put Your Records On, inspired by her multi-platinum hit song. Celebrate the joy of music in this super chilled Sunday session, and hear the story of Bea: a young girl who discovers her great-aunt’s attic is stocked with songs for every single mood.

events.title: The Last Hurrah with Mama G
events.blurb: Join pantomime dame, and author, Mama G for a fabulous story time and parade, to celebrate the end of another amazing children's programme.  Kids of all ages are invited to bring their brightest smiles to our colourful, joyful carnival and party all around the festival site. Let's spread some happiness!

events.title: Unicorn Boy with Dave Roman
events.blurb: Would you like to meet a brilliant comic creator whose brain is like a high-speed blender of ideas? Have you ever wondered what would happen if an ordinary kid grew a massive unicorn horn?! Then it’s time for you to meet author-illustrator Dave Roman, coming to the Festival from New York with his latest creation: Unicorn Boy and the Slumber Party of Doom. Get ready for magic, talking muffins, and very unlikely heroes.

events.title: Cal Flyn & J C Niala: The World Beyond Ourselves
events.blurb: What does it mean to live alongside nature? Why do humans seek it out? Can we balance our need for wilderness with our desire for community? Cal Flyn and J C Niala reflect on these questions in their books. In The Savage Landscape, journalist Flyn (author of Islands of Abandonment) explores humanity’s relationship with wilderness; in The New Eden, award-winning nature writer Niala celebrates the nature in our cities. Together, they discuss their visions for the future. Chaired by David Farrier.

events.title: Anita Anand & William Dalrymple: Empire Podcast – Live
events.blurb: Terrific storytellers and co-hosts of the Empire podcast series, Anita Anand and William Dalrymple are experts at getting to the heart of some of history’s biggest power struggles, from the British Empire to the Ottomans and Ancient India. Today the pair take you behind the scenes, chatting about what goes into writing their hit podcast, and reflecting on times when their research into the past has led them to change their minds and reframe their relationship with history.

events.title: Philippe Sands & Colm Tóibín: Remembering the Dirty War
events.blurb: From 1976 until 1983, the Argentine military junta’s Dirty War was a brutal campaign of violence – tens of thousands of citizens ‘disappeared’, murdered by the state. 50 years on, join Brooklyn author Colm Tóibín – whose 1996 novel, The Story of the Night, was inspired by his own experiences in Argentina – and international lawyer and East West Street author Philippe Sands as they consider the long-lasting impact of the war.

events.title: Cynan Jones: Pulse
events.blurb: Master of the short form and winner of the BBC National Short Story Award Cynan Jones returns to the Festival with his precise and compelling collection of stories, Pulse. Jones explores the realities of life in the working countryside with an intimacy born of experience, alert to the struggle between people and nature. In this radiant conversation, Jones discusses the highs and lows – isolation, peril, but also connection and unexpected joy – of a rural life. Chaired by Dan Richards.

events.title: End of Festival Kids Party
events.blurb: Phew… we made it! We’ve chatted, read, listened, and even danced for the entire Festival, and now it’s time to party. Join us for some games, songs, and a chance to tell us what you liked best, and what you’d like to happen next year. You never know, your idea could make it into a future Book Festival! Featuring Sarah Bowie.

events.title: Junk Journaling: A Workshop with Rachel Hazell
events.blurb: Explore the Festival’s overarching Changing Your Mind theme through the art of junk journaling: transforming discarded ephemera into beautiful books. With bookbinder Rachel Hazell, engage in mindful making through collage and chat through the many benefits (neurological and otherwise) of creative, repetitive tasks like book making. Materials are provided, though you’re invited to bring your own ‘found handwriting’ (old shopping lists, birthday cards, etc) to work with.

events.title: Patrick Ryan: Buckeye
events.blurb: Patrick Ryan’s astonishing debut novel Buckeye earned him comparisons to J D Salinger and William Faulkner – and highest praise from his close friend Ann Patchett, who chairs this special event. Set in a small Ohio town, the novel traces the far-reaching consequences of a stolen moment of passion as they ripple through generations shaped by war, grief, and longing. This unforgettable conversation will explore intimacy, secrecy, forgiveness, desire, and writing lives entangled by history.

events.title: André Aciman & Sarah Maxwell-McNicol: Call Me by Your Name
events.blurb: André Aciman’s million-copy bestseller, Call Me by Your Name, was adapted for the screen to Oscar-winning success by James Ivory in 2017. Now, artist Sarah Maxwell-McNicol gives new life to this moving story of first love through a gorgeously illustrated graphic novel. Aciman and Maxwell-McNicol reflect today on their co-creation process, bringing existing characters to life in new ways, and what goes into adapting a beloved queer cult classic for new audiences. Chaired by Andrés N Ordorica.

events.title: Elizabeth McCracken & John Yorke: The Rules of the Game
events.blurb: What makes a story work? Elizabeth McCracken’s gloriously contrarian A Long Game tears up the rulebook of fiction writing, while John Yorke’s Trip to the Moon uncovers the hidden narrative structures powering everything from beach reads to political propaganda. McCracken, a beloved teacher and author of The Giant’s House joins the legendary story expert and author of Into the Woods, Yorke, for a sparky, illuminating conversation on craft, instinct, form, and the unruly power of a well-told tale. Chaired by Chris Power.

events.title: Madeline Cash & Angela Tomaski: Ruin Runs in the Family
events.blurb: Family legends, open marriages, sibling chaos, criminal conspiracies: two standout debut novelists bring riotous new energy to the family saga. Taking us from a crumbling English manor to an imploding American household – and finding love, absurdity, and catastrophe in both – Angela Tomaski’s The Infamous Gilberts and Madeline Cash’s Lost Lambs open up a lively, hilarious conversation about inheritance, kinship, and mining comedy from the messiest, most intimate corners of family life. Chaired by Catherine Wilson Garry.

events.title: Natsuo Kirino: Swallows
events.blurb: Natsuo Kirino’s complex feminist noir crime novels have awarded her cult status in Japan and abroad. Her latest, Swallows, follows a woman led by economic desperation to become a surrogate mother, and an infertile couple desperate to pass on their ‘elite’ genes. Kirsty Logan leads this incisive conversation with one of Japan’s literary lights about bodily autonomy, the injustices of class and gender, and what it means to be ‘in control’.

events.title: Maggie O’Farrell: Land
events.blurb: Beginning on a windswept peninsula on the west of Ireland and charting a journey spanning generations, Land is Maggie O’Farrell’s most ambitious novel to date. Following an Oscar nomination for the poignant screenplay of her novel Hamnet, O’Farrell discusses this epic new tale of colonisation and rebellion inspired by family history. We knew it already, but Land cements O’Farrell’s status as one of our finest writers working today. Chaired by Sam Baker.

events.title: For the Love of Agnes: A Celebration of Agnes Owens
events.blurb: Agnes Owens was a writer’s writer, beloved by all from James Kelman to Liz Lochhead for her guileless prose and mastery of what Ali Smith called the ‘deadpan gothic’. In her centenary year, publisher Birlinn introduce Owens to a new generation of readers with special editions of her most-loved books. Booker Prize-winner Douglas Stuart, and William Letford come together to celebrate the life and writing of one of Scotland’s singular undersung talents. Roxani Krystalli has now joined the panel. Chaired by Chitra Ramaswamy.

events.title: The Fun Lovin Crime Writers
events.blurb: 'Murdering songs for fun in front of anyone who will listen’ is how this crime-writing super-group describe themselves. Tonight, they return to the scene of the crime: our Spiegeltent, where they performed their very first gig. Join Mark Billingham, Chris Brookmyre, Doug Johnstone, Stuart Neville, Val McDermid, and Luca Veste as the group swap their desks for the stage and put on an unmissable, riotous evening of rock and roll to close out this year's festival.
